then the ministers falsely claim ability.
If the ruler desires to see,
then the ministers' true feelings and appearances obtain their capital.
Therefore, Zǐ Zhī relied on the virtuous
to usurp his lord,
Shù Diāo and
Yì Yá took advantage of their ruler's desires
to encroach upon their ruler.
In the end, Zǐ Kuài died in chaos,
and Duke Huán's worms flowed out of his door
and he was not buried.
What is the reason for this?
It is the trouble of the ruler lending his feelings to his ministers.
The feelings of ministers do not necessarily love their ruler;
it is for the sake of great profit.
Now, if the ruler does not conceal his feelings,
does not hide his intentions,
and allows ministers to have opportunities
to encroach upon their lord,
then for the ministers to become Zǐ Zhī or
Tián Cháng 田常 will not be difficult to deal with.
Therefore, it is said:
"Eliminate likes and dislikes,
and the ministers will reveal their true nature."
When the ministers reveal their true nature,
then the ruler will not be deceived.
Chapter Eight: Exalting Power
Heaven has its great destiny,
and man has his great destiny.
Now, fragrant, delicious, and crisp flavors,
rich wine and fatty meat,
please the mouth but harm the body;
graceful carriage and white teeth
please the emotions but deplete the essence.
Therefore, eliminate excess and extravagance,
and the body will be unharmed.
Power should not be displayed;
be naturally non-assertive.
Affairs are managed throughout the realm,
but the essential is in the center.
The sage grasps the essential,
and the four directions will follow his example.
Remain empty and await them;
they will naturally bring themselves.
When the four seas are secure,
The Way of Yin is made visible by Yang.
When left and right are established,
Open the gate and be ready.
Do not change, do not alter;
Proceed with both together;
To proceed without ceasing,
This is called treading the principle.
Now, things have their proper suitability,
Talents have their proper application.
Each resides in its proper place,
Therefore, the ruler is without action (wú wéi).
Employ the rooster to keep watch at night,
Command the wildcat to catch mice;
All are employed according to their abilities,
And so the ruler has nothing to do.
If the ruler has particular strengths,
Affairs will not be impartial.
If one is boastful and fond of ability,
He will be deceived by those below;
If one is eloquent and fond of generating (ideas),
Those below will take advantage of his talents.
When superiors and inferiors exchange roles,
The state will not be governed well.
The Way of using the One:
Naming is the foremost consideration.
When names are correct,
things are settled.
When names are unreliable,
things shift.
Therefore, the Sage holds to the One in stillness,
causing names to arise of themselves,
and allowing affairs to settle themselves.
Not displaying his own talents,
his inferiors will therefore be genuinely upright.
Following circumstances and entrusting them,
causing them to manage their own affairs;
following circumstances and giving to them,
they will then naturally exalt themselves;
dealing with them in an upright manner,
causing them all to settle themselves.
The ruler uses names to manage them,
not focusing on their forms,
but rather cultivates their character.
When form and name correspond and agree,
use them according to their innate nature.
When these two are genuinely trustworthy,
inferiors will then present their true feelings.
Carefully cultivate one's affairs,
Awaiting the decree of Heaven.
Do not lose its essence,
Then one becomes a sage.
The Way of the sage is
To discard wisdom and skill.
If wisdom and skill are not discarded,
It is difficult to make them constant.
If the common people employ them,
Their bodies will suffer much misfortune.
If the ruler employs them,
His state will be in peril of destruction.
Relying on the Way of Heaven,
Reversing the principles of form,
Supervise, examine, and investigate them thoroughly;
When the end comes, there will be a beginning.
Emptiness and stillness come after;
Never employing oneself.
All the troubles of those above
Must have the same origin.
Believe but do not conform;
Ten thousand people will follow as one.
Now, the Dào (道)
Is vast and without form,
Dé (德)
Is a thorough principle and universally reaches.
As for all living things,
Carefully consider and employ it;
All things will flourish,
But do not participate in their tranquility.
Dao
descends and encompasses affairs,
investigating and assigning tasks accordingly,
living and dying with the times.
Compare names and differentiate tasks,
connect and unify emotions.
Therefore, it is said:
Dao is different from the myriad things,
Dé (德) is different from Yīn (陰) and Yáng (陽),
a balance is different from light and heavy,
a plumb line is different from going out and coming in,
harmony is different from dryness and moisture,
a ruler is different from his subjects.
All these six are
manifestations of Dao.
Dao is without equal,
therefore it is called one.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler values the appearance of solitary Dao.
If the ruler and his ministers follow different paths,
the subordinates use names to petition,
The ruler grasps the name (míng),
the ministers emulate the form (xíng).
When form and name correspond,
superiors and inferiors are in harmony.
In general, the way to listen
is to take what they put forth
and turn it back to them as entry.
Therefore, scrutinize the name to fix its position,
clarify distinctions to differentiate categories.
The way to listen to words
is to be as if thoroughly drunk.
Lips before teeth?
I will not be the one to initiate it.
Teeth before lips?
It becomes increasingly muddled.
When they separate themselves,
I then use this to understand them.
When rights and wrongs converge,
the ruler does not participate in the construction (of arguments).
Vacant, tranquil, and non-acting:
this is the essence of the Way (Dào).
Comparing and classifying things
is the form of affairs.
Compare them in order to classify things;
classify them in order to join them to emptiness (xū).
If the fundamental root is not reformed,
then actions will be leaked without loss.
Dissolve them in action,
attack them with non-action.
If you delight in them,
there will be much to do;
if you hate them,
resentment will arise.
Therefore, discard joy and discard hatred,
make your heart empty as a dwelling for the Dao.
If the ruler does not share the profits with them,
the people will favor him;
if the ruler does not share the righteousness with them,
he can make them act alone.
If the ruler firmly closes the inner bolt,
observing the courtyard from within the room,
everything within a short distance is present,
and everyone goes to their appropriate place.
Reward with reward,
punish with punishment,
based on what they do,
each achieves themselves.
Good and evil will inevitably reach them,
who would dare not believe it?
Once standards are established,
The three corners are thus arranged.
If the ruler is not discerning,
the subordinates will have their reasons (for doing things);
if affairs are not handled properly,
the subordinates will examine the normal course of things.
Like heaven and earth,
this is called a release from burdens.
If earth and heaven,
who is distant and who is close?
To be able to resemble heaven and earth,
is called a sage.
If you wish to govern the inner realm,
establish it and do not get personally involved;
if you wish to govern the outer realm,
establish one official,
do not let him act arbitrarily,
how then can encroachment and usurpation occur?
At the gate of great ministers,
one should only fear having too many people.
In all extreme governance,
the lower levels are unable to obtain (advantage).
If punishments and titles are applied comprehensively,
the people will then adhere to their duties;
to abandon this and seek something else,
This is called great delusion.
The cunning people become more numerous,
treachery and evil fill the surroundings.
Therefore, it is said:
Do not enrich a man and then lend to him,
do not ennoble a man and then coerce him,
do not solely trust one person and lose your capital and state.
If the calf is larger than the thigh,
it is difficult to run quickly.
If the ruler loses his spirit,
a tiger will follow behind him.
If the ruler above does not know this,
the tiger will become like a dog.
If the ruler does not stop it early,
the dog will become increasingly unrestrained.
The tiger will form its pack,
in order to kill its mother.
To be a ruler and have no subjects,
what state will there be?
If the ruler implements his laws,
the great tiger will become timid;
if the ruler implements his punishments,
the great tiger will become peaceful on its own.
If laws and punishments are truly trusted,
The tiger transforms into a man,
only to revert to its true form.
If you wish to govern its country,
you must destroy its gatherings;
if you do not destroy its gatherings,
it will amass followers.
If you wish to manage its land,
you must appropriately distribute its resources;
if you do not appropriately distribute its resources,
disorderly people will seek to profit.
If they demand and I grant,
it is like handing an axe to an enemy;
if it is unacceptable to hand it over,
they will use it to attack me.
Huángdì has a saying:
"The ruler and the ruled fight a hundred battles a day."
The ruled conceal their private interests,
and use them to test their ruler;
the ruler wields standards of measurement,
to control the ruled.
Therefore, the establishment of standards of measurement [dù liáng],
is a treasure for the ruler;
the formation of factions,
is a treasure for the minister.
The reason why ministers do not assassinate their rulers
Cliques and factions should not be tolerated.
Therefore, if the ruler loses by a *fú cùn* (
very small unit), those below will gain by a *xún cháng* (larger unit).
A ruler who possesses a state
should not make his capital too large;
a minister who follows the Way
should not enrich his family.
A ruler who follows the Way
does not esteem his ministers too highly.
Esteem them and enrich them,
and they will replace him.
To prepare against danger and fear peril,
promptly establish a crown prince,
then calamity will have no way to arise.
Investigating within the enclosure (of your own state) to eliminate those who escape its boundaries,
one must personally hold the standard of measurement.
For those who are too rich, reduce them;
for those who are too poor, enrich them.
Reducing and enriching must have a standard,
do not allow the people to form factions
and collude to deceive their superiors.
Reduce like the waning moon,
enrich like the heat.
Simplify commands, be cautious in punishment,
Punishment must be carried out to its fullest extent.
Do not relax your bow,
for one perch cannot accommodate two males.
One perch cannot accommodate two males,
their fighting will be fierce.
If jackals and wolves are in the pen,
the sheep will not thrive.
If one family has two nobles,
affairs will surely be without merit.
If husband and wife hold government,
the son will have nowhere to turn.
He who is a ruler
should frequently prune his trees,
and not allow the branches to spread sparsely.
If the branches spread sparsely,
they will block the public gate (gōng lǘ),
private doors will be filled,
the public court will be empty,
and the ruler will be besieged.
Frequently prune your trees,
do not allow the branches to resist outward;
if the branches resist outward,
they will press upon the ruler's dwelling.
Frequently prune the tree,
do not let the branches become large while the trunk is small;
if the branches become large while the trunk is small,
it will not withstand the spring wind;
if it cannot withstand the spring wind,
the branches will harm the heartwood.
When the young lords are numerous,
the royal clan will murmur with anxiety.
The way to stop this is to
frequently prune the tree,
not allowing the branches to flourish.
If the tree is frequently pruned,
then factions will separate.
Dig up its root
and stem,
then the tree will no longer be strong.
Fill in its surging abyss,
do not let the water be clear.
Probe their thoughts,
take away their authority.
If the ruler uses these methods,
it will be like lightning and thunder.
Eight Villainies, Ninth
Generally speaking, there are eight methods by which ministers can become villainous:
there are eight arts:
First is being "in the same bed."
What is meant by "in the same bed?"
It means:
Favored wives,
beloved young children,
those who are indulged in ease and pleasure and fond of sexual gratification,
these are what confuse a ruler.
Taking advantage of moments of leisure and repose,
exploiting times of drunkenness and satiety,
to seek what they desire,
this is a technique to certainly be listened to.
For those who are ministers, they serve them internally with gold and jade,
causing them to confuse their ruler,
this is what is called "in the same bed."
Second is being "at the side."
What is meant by "at the side?"
It means:
Jesters and dwarfs,
close attendants on the left and right,
these are the ones who say "yes, yes" before the ruler has given an order,
who answer "yes, yes" before being instructed,
anticipating the ruler's intent,
observing his appearance and discerning his mood
to be ahead of the ruler's thoughts.
These all advance and retreat together,
They all respond and all agree;
with one voice and aligned purpose,
they shift the ruler's mind.
Those who serve as ministers
internally serve him with gold, jade, playthings, and rarities;
externally, they act unlawfully for him,
causing him to transform his lord.
This is called "being at his side".
Third is *fù xiōng* (father-elder brother).
What is meant by *fù xiōng*?
It means:
concubines and princes of the side chambers
whom the ruler cherishes and loves;
great ministers and court officials
with whom the ruler deliberates and plans.
All these exert their efforts and exhaust their counsel,
and the ruler is sure to listen to them.
Those who serve as ministers serve the princes and concubines with music, women, and children;
they win over great ministers and court officials with words;
they handle confidential matters and report on affairs;
if matters succeed, they advance ranks and increase emoluments
to encourage their hearts
and cause them to offend their ruler.
This is called *fù xiōng*.
Fourth is nourishing calamity.
What is meant by nourishing calamity?
It means:
When a ruler delights in beautiful palaces, terraces, and ponds,
and enjoys adorning his sons and daughters, dogs and horses to please his heart,
this is a calamity for the ruler.
When ministers exhaust the people's strength
to beautify palaces, terraces, and ponds,
and heavily tax and collect
to adorn sons and daughters, dogs and horses,
to please their ruler and confuse his mind,
following his desires,
and establishing private gains in the midst of it,
this is called "nourishing calamity" (yǎng yāng).
Fifth is popular support.
What is meant by popular support?
It means:
When ministers distribute public wealth to please the people,
practice small favors to win over the common people,
so that the court and the marketplace all praise him,
to block his lord and accomplish his own desires,
this is called "popular support" (mín méng).
Sixth is prevalence.
What is meant by prevalence?
It means:
The ruler of men,
is naturally prone to blocking words and discussion,
rarely listening to debates and arguments,
and easily swayed by persuasive rhetoric.
Those who are ministers
seek out debaters from the feudal lords,
nurture eloquent speakers within the state,
and have them speak in their private interests.
They create skillfully crafted writings,
and popular expressions,
showing the ruler advantages and power,
frightening them with dangers and harms,
employing deceptive language to corrupt their lord.
This is called "circulation" (liú xíng).
Seventh is coercive power (wēi qiáng).
What is coercive power (wēi qiáng)?
It means:
the ruler of men,
takes the assembled ministers and the common people
as the source of their coercive power (wēi qiáng).
What the assembled ministers and the common people deem good,
the ruler deems good;
what the assembled ministers and the common people deem not good,
the ruler deems not good.
Being a subject,
gathering sword-bearing retainers,
raising soldiers ready to die,
in order to display one's power,
making it clear that those who work for oneself will surely benefit,
and those who do not work for oneself will surely die,
in order to intimidate the officials and common people
and carry out one's own selfish desires;
this is called "wei qiáng" (威強, forceful strength).
Eight is the realm of the four directions.
What are the four directions?
It is said:
For those who rule,
if the state is small,
then serve the large state;
if the army is weak,
then fear the strong army.
What the large state demands,
the small state must listen to;
where the strong army attacks,
the weak army must submit.
Being a subject,
heavily taxing the people,
emptying the treasury,
weakening the state to serve the large state,
and use their power to seek to entice their ruler;
in severe cases, they raise troops to gather at the border
and impose levies internally;
in less severe cases, they frequently send grand envoys to intimidate their ruler,
causing them to be fearful.
This is what is called "all directions" (`sìfāng`).
All these eight,
are the ways by which subjects accomplish their treachery,
by which the rulers of the world are obstructed and coerced,
and lose what they possess,
one cannot but examine them closely.
A wise ruler, in dealing with those within,
enjoys their beauty but does not act upon their solicitations,
and does not allow private requests.
In dealing with those on the left and right,
he makes their person responsible for their words,
and does not allow them to add words.
In dealing with his father, elder brothers, and great ministers,
when listening to their words, he must make them responsible with punishment
afterward,
and does not allow them to act recklessly.
In dealing with spectacles, amusements, and precious objects,
he must order them to come from a certain source,
and does not allow them to be brought in or taken out at will,
He does not allow his ministers to speculate about his intentions.
In matters of virtuous actions and bestowing benefits,
even if it means relaxing restrictions on wealth,
opening granaries,
anything beneficial to the people
must originate from the ruler;
he does not allow his ministers to privately claim credit for his virtue.
In matters of persuasion and discussion,
those who praise are rewarded for what they are good at,
those who criticize are punished for what they are bad at,
he must verify their abilities,
and observe their faults,
not allowing ministers to speak on each other's behalf.
As for brave and strong warriors,
military achievements in war are rewarded without fail,
but acts of violence within the city are punished without pardon;
he does not allow his ministers to use private wealth.
As for the demands of the various feudal lords,
if they accord with the laws, he listens to them;
if they do not accord with the laws, he rejects them.
The so-called "lost ruler"
is not necessarily one who has no state,
but rather one whose state, although he possesses it,
is not truly his own.
To allow ministers
to control affairs internally from the outside,
this means the ruler is ruined.
To listen to a large state for the sake of saving the country from ruin,
and ruin comes more quickly than not listening,
therefore, one does not listen.
When the assembled ministers know that one does not listen,
then they will not rely on the feudal lords from the outside;
When the feudal lords know that one does not listen,
then they will not accept the ministers' slander of their ruler.
The reason why an enlightened ruler establishes official positions, ranks, and stipends
is to promote men of virtue and talent and to encourage those with merit.
Therefore it is said:
Men of virtue and talent occupy high positions and receive generous stipends;
they hold important offices;
those with great merit receive honored ranks
and receive substantial rewards.
When evaluating officials with virtue, their abilities are measured;
when allocating stipends, their achievements are weighed.
Because of this, men of virtue do not misrepresent their abilities
in serving their lord,
those with merit gladly advance their careers,
and therefore affairs are successfully managed and achievements are established.
But now it is not like this.
Not assessing the worthy or unworthy,
not considering meritorious service,
wielding the authority of the feudal lords,
heeding the solicitations of those on the left and right.
Fathers, elder brothers, and senior ministers petition the ruler above for titles and emoluments,
and then sell them below to amass wealth and profit,
as well as to establish private factions.
Therefore, those with abundant wealth buy official positions to become noble,
and those with connections to those on the left and right
use solicitations to attain prominence.
Meritorious ministers are disregarded,
and the promotions of officials are erroneous and flawed.
Therefore, officials neglect their duties
and engage in external affairs,
abandoning their responsibilities and embracing wealth.
Because of this, the worthy become lax and unmotivated,
and the meritorious become discouraged and neglect their duties.
This is the way of a collapsing state.
Ten Faults, Chapter Ten
Ten Faults:
First, practicing minor loyalty
is a detriment to great loyalty.
Second, caring for small gains
destroys great benefits.
Third, being unconventional and self-willed,
To be discourteous to the feudal lords
is the height of self-destruction.
Fourthly, to not focus on governance
but to indulge in music,
is a lifelong pursuit of destitution.
Fifthly, to be greedy, obstinate, and fond of profit
is the root of destroying the state and killing oneself.
Sixthly, to indulge in female entertainment
and disregard state affairs
is a disaster that leads to the destruction of the state.
Seventhly, to abandon internal affairs and travel far afield,
while neglecting the advice of counselors,
is a path to endangering oneself.
Eighthly, to err and not listen to loyal ministers,
but to act solely on one's own will,
is to destroy one's great reputation
and the beginning of being laughed at.
Ninthly, to not assess one's own strength internally
and to rely on the feudal lords externally
is a calamity that leads to the weakening of the state.
Tenthly, for a small state to be discourteous
and not employ ministers who offer remonstrance
is a situation that leads to the end of its lineage.
What is meant by "minor loyalty"?
Formerly, King Gòng of Chǔ and Duke Lì of Jìn
fought at Yānlíng.
The Chǔ army was defeated,
and King Gòng was wounded in the eye.
In the heat of battle,
Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn was thirsty and asked for a drink.
The attendant Gǔyáng held a cup of wine and offered it to him.
Zǐfǎn said,
"Hey,
take it away!
It's wine."
Gǔyáng said,
"It is not wine."
Zǐfǎn accepted it and drank it.
Zǐfǎn's character was such that he
loved wine
and found it sweet.
He could not keep it from his mouth,
and became drunk.
After the battle ended,
King Gòng wanted to resume fighting.
He ordered someone to summon Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn.
Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn declined, citing a heart ailment.
King Gòng rode there himself,
Entering his tent,
he smelled the stench of wine and returned,
saying:
"In today's battle,
I, myself, was wounded.
The one I rely on
is the Sīmǎ.
Yet the Sīmǎ is so drunk,
this is to destroy the altars of the Chǔ kingdom
and to not care for our multitudes.
I will not fight again."
Thereupon he withdrew his army and departed,
executing Sīmǎ Zǐfǎn as a great punishment.
Therefore, Shù Gǔyáng's offering of wine
was not intended to harm Zǐfǎn,
his heart was loyal and loving towards him,
but it just happened to kill him.
Therefore it is said:
Practicing small loyalty
is the enemy of great loyalty.
What is meant by being concerned with small advantages?
In the past, Duke Xiàn of Jìn wished to borrow a road through Yú
in order to attack Guó.
Xún Xī said:
"Your Lordship should use the jade of Chuíjí and the carriage from Qūchǎn
to bribe the Duke of Yú,
asking to borrow a road.
He will certainly lend us the road."
The Lord said:
"The jade of Chuíjí,
is a treasure of my late lord;
the chariot of Qūchǎn,
is my finest horse.
If he accepts our gifts but does not grant us passage,
what shall we do?"
Xún Xī said:
"If he does not grant us passage,
he will certainly not dare to accept our gifts.
If he accepts our gifts and grants us passage,
then it is like taking treasures from the inner treasury
and storing them in the outer treasury,
like taking horses from the inner stable
and placing them in the outer stable.
Your Lordship, do not worry."
The Lord said:
"Agreed."
Thereupon he sent Xún Xī to bribe Lord Yú with the jade of Chuíjí and the chariot of Qūchǎn,
and request passage through his territory.
Lord Yú, greedy for the jade and the horses, desired to grant the request.
Gōng Zhīqí advised, saying:
"It cannot be permitted.
The relationship between Yú and Guó
is like a carriage having a guard rail.
The guard rail depends on the carriage,
and the carriage also depends on the guard rail.
The power dynamic between Yú and Guó is precisely this.
If we lend them a path,
then Guó will perish in the morning, and Yú will follow it in the evening.
It is not permissible;
I wish you would not allow it."
The Duke of Yú did not listen to him
and subsequently lent them the path.
Xún Xī attacked Guó and conquered it.
He returned and remained there for three years.
Then, he raised an army to attack Yú,
and conquered it again.
Xún Xī led the horse and held the jade
to report to Duke Xiàn.
Duke Xiàn was pleased and said:
"The jade is still the same.
However,
the horse's teeth have also grown longer."
Therefore, the reason why the Duke of Yú's army was weakened
As for the diminishment of territory,
what is the reason?
It is loving small advantages and not considering their harm.
Therefore, it is said:
Focusing on small advantages
results in the ruin of great advantages.
What is meant by "deviant conduct"?
In the past, when Chǔ Língwáng hosted the assembly at Shēn,
the Crown Prince of Sòng arrived late,
and he was seized and imprisoned.
He became intimate with the lord of Xú
and detained Qí Qìngfēng.
The middle-ranking archer advised him, saying:
"In assembling the feudal lords, one cannot be without propriety;
this is a matter of survival or destruction.
In the past, when Jié hosted the assembly at Yǒuróng,
Yǒumín rebelled against him.
When Zhòu held the hunt at Líqiū,
the Róng
and Dí rebelled against him.
This was due to a lack of propriety.
Your Majesty, please consider this."
The ruler did not listen
and proceeded to carry out his own will.
In less than a year,
Líng Wáng traveled south,
and his ministers followed him and kidnapped him.
Líng Wáng starved to death on the banks of the Qián Stream.
Therefore, it is said:
Acting perversely and being self-willed,
and showing no courtesy to the feudal lords,
is the ultimate path to ruin.
What is meant by "fond of music"?
Once, Wèi Línggōng was about to go to Jìn,
and when he arrived at the banks of the Pú River,
he unharnessed his carriages and released his horses,
setting up lodging to stay overnight.
In the middle of the night,
he heard the sound of a new drum melody and was delighted by it.
He sent people to ask those around him,
but all reported that they had not heard it.
He then summoned Shī Juān and told him,
"There is a new drum melody,
and I sent people to ask those around me,
but all reported that they had not heard it.
Its form seems like that of ghosts and spirits,
I want you to listen and transcribe it for me."
Shī Juān said,
"Yes."
Written because of quiet sitting and playing the qin.
Shī Juān reported the next day, saying:
"Your servant has obtained it,
but has not yet mastered it.
Please allow me to stay another night to practice it."
Líng Gōng said:
"Agreed."
So he stayed another night.
The next day,
he had mastered it,
and then departed for Jìn.
Duke Píng of Jìn feasted him at the Terrace of Shī Yí.
In the midst of the wine,
Líng Gōng arose.
The duke said:
"There is a new melody,
and I wish to present it."
Duke Píng said:
"Good."
Then he summoned Shī Juān,
ordering him to sit beside Shī Kuàng,
to take up the qin and play it.
Before he finished,
Shī Kuàng stopped him with his hand,
saying:
"This is the sound of a state's downfall,
it should not be continued."
Píng Gōng said:
"From where does this melody originate?"
Shī Kuàng said:
"This was composed by Shī Yán,
who made licentious music for Zhòu.
When Wǔ Wáng attacked Zhòu,
Shī Yán fled east,
and drowned himself in the River Pú.
Therefore, whoever hears this sound
must be above the River Pú.
Whoever hears this sound first,
their state will surely be diminished,
it should not be continued."
Píng Gōng said:
"What I love
is music,
you should allow it to continue."
Shī Juān continued to play it to the end.
Píng Gōng asked Shī Kuàng:
"What is this melody called?"
Shī Kuàng said:
"This is called Qīng Shāng."
The Duke said:
"Is the *Qīngshāng* tune truly the most sorrowful?"
Shī Kuàng said:
"It is not as sorrowful as the *Qīngzhǐ*."
The Duke said:
"Can the *Qīngzhǐ* be heard?"
Shī Kuàng said:
"It cannot.
In ancient times, those who listened to the *Qīngzhǐ*
were all lords with virtue and righteousness.
Now, my lord's virtue is shallow,
and is not sufficient to hear it."
Duke Píng said:
"What I love
is music,
I wish to try to listen to it."
Shī Kuàng, having no choice,
took up the zither and played it.
Once he played it,
there were sixteen black cranes
coming from the south,
gathered at the ruined gate of the palace.
He played it again,
and they lined up.
After playing three times,
it stretched its neck and sang,
spread its wings and danced.
The sound was in tune with the gōng and shāng tones,
and the sound was heard in Heaven.
Píng Gōng was greatly pleased,
and all who were seated rejoiced.
Píng Gōng raised his wine cup
and stood up to offer a toast to Shī Kuàng,
then sat back down and asked,
"Is there any sound more sorrowful than the qīng zhǐ?"
Shī Kuàng said,
"Not as sorrowful as the qīng jiǎo."
Píng Gōng said,
"Can the qīng jiǎo be heard?"
Shī Kuàng said,
"No.
In the past, Huángdì united the ghosts and spirits
on Mount Tài,
riding an elephant carriage pulled by six jiaolong dragons,
with bìfāng birds alongside the linchpins,
Chī Yóu leading the way,
the Wind Earl advancing to sweep the path,
the Rain Master sprinkling the road,
tigers and wolves in front,
Ghosts and spirits are behind,
the *téngshé* serpent lies on the ground,
the phoenix covers from above,
a great confluence of ghosts and spirits,
resulting in the *qīng jiǎo* music.
Now, my lord, your virtue is thin,
insufficient to listen to it.
To listen to it,
I fear there will be defeat."
Duke Píng said:
"I am old,
what I love is music,
I wish to listen to it."
Shī Kuàng had no choice but to play it.
Once he played it,
dark clouds rose from the northwest;
again he played it,
a great wind arrived,
great rain followed it,
tearing the curtains,
breaking the sacrificial vessels,
destroying the tiles of the corridor.
Those sitting scattered and fled,
Duke Píng was frightened,
Lay prostrate between the corridors.
The Jìn Guó (晉國) state suffered a great drought,
the land was barren for three years.
Duke Píng (平公)'s body consequently became crippled and ill.
Therefore it is said:
If one does not attend to governance,
and indulges endlessly in the five musical tones,
then it will be a lifelong affliction.
What is meant by greed and obstinacy?
In the past, Zhì Bó Yáo (智伯瑤) led the Zhao (趙),
Han (韓), and Wei (魏)
to attack Fan (范) and
Zhōng Háng (中行),
and destroyed them.
Returning,
he rested his troops for several years,
then sent someone to request territory from Han (韓).
Hán Kāngzǐ (韓康子) wanted not to give it,
but Duàn Guī (段規) advised,
"It is not permissible to not give it.
For Zhì Bó's (知伯) character is such that
he loves profit and is arrogant and obstinate.
If he comes to request territory and is not given it,
then he will surely move his troops against Han (韓).
Your lord should give it to him.
If you give it to him, he will become emboldened.
He will then ask other states for land.
If other states refuse,
refuse,
then Zhī Bó 智伯 will surely increase his military pressure on them.
If that happens,
Hán 韓 can avoid trouble
and await the changes in the situation."
Kāngzǐ 康子 said:
"Agreed."
He then ordered an envoy to present one district with ten thousand households
to Zhī Bó 智伯.
Zhī Bó 智伯 was pleased
and sent someone to ask Wèi 魏 for land.
Xuānzǐ 宣子 wanted to refuse.
Zhào Jiā 趙葭 advised,
"He asked Hán 韓 for land,
and Hán 韓 gave it to him.
Now he is asking Wèi 魏 for land.
If Wèi 魏 does not give it to him,
it means that Wèi 魏 is strong internally
and angers Zhī Bó 智伯 externally.
If you do not give it to him,
he will surely deploy troops against Wèi 魏.
"It would be better to give it to him."
Xuānzǐ said:
"Agreed."
So he sent someone to deliver a county with ten thousand households
to Zhībó.
Zhībó then sent someone to Zhao to request the land of Cài
and Gāoláng,
which Zhào Xiāngzǐ did not give.
Thereupon Zhībó secretly made an agreement with Hán and Wèi,
intending to attack Zhao.
Xiāngzǐ summoned Zhāng Mèngtán and told him,
"As for Zhībó's character,
he is outwardly friendly but inwardly distant.
He has sent three envoys to Hán and Wèi,
and I have not agreed with him,
he will surely deploy troops against me.
Where can I safely reside?"
Zhāng Mèngtán said:
"Dǒng Èyú was
a talented minister of Lord Jian,
he governed Jìnyáng,
and Yǐn Duó followed his example,
and his remaining teachings still exist,
your lord should definitely reside in Jìnyáng only."
The lord said,
"Agreed."
Thereupon he summoned Yánlíng Shēng,
ordering him to lead the chariots and cavalry
to Jìnyáng first,
and the lord followed after him.
When the lord arrived,
he inspected the city walls and the stores of the five offices.
The city walls were not well maintained,
the granaries had no stored grain,
the treasuries had no stored money,
the armories had no armor and weapons,
and the towns had no defensive equipment.
Xiāngzǐ was afraid,
and summoned Zhāng Mèngtán, saying,
"I have inspected the city walls
and the stores of the five offices,
and all are ill-prepared.
How shall I respond to the enemy?"
Zhāng Mèngtán said,
"Your servant has heard that the government of a sage
is stored in the people,
not stored in treasuries and armories;
focus on cultivating education,
not maintaining city walls.
Your Lordship should issue an order,
ordering the people to save enough food for three years,
and those who have surplus grain should deposit it in the granary;
save enough supplies for three years of use,
and those who have surplus money should deposit it in the treasury;
and if there are extraordinary talents remaining,
have them manage the repair of the city walls."
The lord issued the order in the evening,
and the next day,
the granaries could not contain all the grain,
the treasury was without accumulated money,
and the armory did not accept weapons and armor.
In five days, the city walls were repaired,
and defenses were fully prepared.
The lord summoned Zhāng Mèngtán 張孟談 and asked him,
"My city walls are already repaired,
defenses are fully prepared,
money and grain are sufficient,
and weapons and armor are abundant,
but what should I do about the lack of arrows?"
Zhāng Mèngtán 張孟談 said,
"I have heard that when Dǒng Zǐ 董子 governed Jìnyáng 晉陽,
the walls of the ducal palace
were all built with reeds, artemisia, arrow shafts, and chaste trees,
There was *kǔ* wood as tall as a *zhàng*.
"Your lord can take and use it."
Thereupon, he took it and tested it.
Its hardness was such that even the strength of the *jūn* and *lù* bamboo
could not surpass it.
The lord said:
"My arrows are already sufficient,
but what to do about the lack of metal?"
Zhāng Mèngtán said:
"I have heard that when Dǒng Zǐ governed Jìnyáng,
the halls of the public palaces and command quarters
all used refined copper as pillars and foundations.
Your lord can take and use them."
Thereupon, he took and used them,
and there was metal in surplus.
Commands were already determined,
and defenses were already prepared.
The troops of the three states indeed arrived.
Upon arrival, they mounted the walls of Jìnyáng
and engaged in battle.
For three months, they were unable to capture it.
Consequently, they relaxed their forces and surrounded it,
managing the waters of Jìnyáng to flood it.
They besieged Jìnyáng for three years.
The people within the city lived in nests and dwelt there,
hanging pots to cook,
wealth and food were about to be exhausted,
the officers and gentlemen were weak and ill.
Xiāng Zǐ said to Zhāng Mèngtán,
"Food supplies are scarce,
financial resources are depleted,
the officers and gentlemen are weak and ill,
I fear we will not be able to defend any longer!
I want to surrender the city,
to what state is it acceptable to surrender?"
Zhāng Mèngtán said,
"I have heard that
if one cannot preserve what is about to perish,
or secure what is in danger,
then there is no use in valuing wisdom.
If you, my lord, abandon this plan,
I ask to try secretly slipping out,
to see the rulers of Hán
and Wèi."
Zhāng Mèngtán saw the rulers of Hán
and Wèi and said,
"I have heard that when the lips are gone, the teeth will be cold.
Now Zhī Bó is leading you two lords to attack Zhào,
Zhao is about to perish.
If Zhao perishes,
then the two lords will be next."
The two lords said:
"I know it is so.
However,
Zhī Bó's character
is rough but insightful, yet he has few intimates.
If our plot is discovered,
then disaster will surely befall us.
What can we do about it?"
Zhāng Mèngtán said:
"The plan will come from the mouths of the two lords,
and enter the ears of your servant,
no one else will know it."
The two lords then agreed with Zhāng Mèngtán
on the revolt of the three armies,
and set a date with him.
That night, they sent Mèngtán into Jìnyáng,
to report the revolt of the two lords.
Xiāngzi welcomed Mèngtán and bowed to him twice,
both fearful and delighted.
The two lords sent Zhāng Mèngtán after the agreement,
and then went to court with Zhī Bó and left,
encountering Zhì Guò outside the gate of the barracks.
Zhì Guò was surprised by their expression,
and therefore went in to see Zhī Bó, saying:
"The two lords' appearance suggests that something is about to change."
The lord said:
"How so?"
He said,
"Their demeanor is haughty and their intentions lofty,
unlike their behavior at other times.
You would do well to act before they do."
Zhī Bó said,
"I have made a careful agreement with the two lords
to conquer Zhào and divide its territory into three parts.
The reason I am so close to them
is that they will certainly not encroach upon or deceive me.
Our troops have been stationed at Jìnyáng for three years,
and we will conquer it morning and night.
They are eager for the gain
so why would they have other intentions?
Surely not.
Put your mind at ease and do not worry,
and do not speak of this to others."
The next morning,
the two lords again came to court and then left,
and Zhì Guò again saw them at the gate.
Zhì Guò entered to see him and said:
"Did you tell the two lords what I said?"
The lord said:
"How did you know?"
He said:
"Today the two lords emerged from court in the morning,
and when they saw me, their expressions changed,
and they kept looking at me.
There must be a change.
It would be better for you to kill them."
The lord said:
"Put this aside and don't speak of it again."
Zhì Guò said:
"No,
you must kill them.
If you cannot kill them,
then you should befriend them."
The lord said:
"How can I befriend them?"
Zhì Guò said:
"The strategist of Wèi Xuānzǐ was called Zhào Jiā,
and the strategist of Hán Kāngzǐ was called Duàn Guī.
These men are all able to alter their lords' plans.
You should make an agreement with the two lords
to destroy the state of Zhao,
and then enfeoff each of these two men
with a county of ten thousand households.
If you do this,
then the minds of the two lords will not change."
Zhī Bó said:
“If we destroy Zhào and divide its territory into three parts,
and then enfeoff each of my two sons
with a county of ten thousand households,
then what I will get will be little.
It cannot be done.”
Zhì Guò, seeing that his words were not being heeded,
departed,
and changed his clan name to Fǔ.
When the appointed day arrived,
the Zhào clan killed the officer guarding the dike
and breached it, flooding Zhī Bó’s army.
Zhī Bó’s army was thrown into chaos trying to control the flood,
Hán and Wèi flanked and attacked them,
and Xiāngzǐ led his soldiers to assault their front.
They greatly defeated Zhī Bó's army
and captured Zhī Bó.
Zhī Bó died and his army was destroyed,
his state was divided into three,
becoming a laughingstock for the world.
Therefore it is said:
Greed, obstinacy, and fondness for profit
are the root of national destruction and personal death.
What is meant by indulging in female entertainment?
In the past, the Róng king sent Yóu Yú
as an envoy to Qín.
Duke Mù asked him, saying:
"I have often heard of the Dao
but have not yet seen it with my own eyes.
I wish to hear how the enlightened rulers of antiquity gained and lost their states."
Yóu Yú replied:
"I have heard of it before:
They always gained them through frugality
and lost them through extravagance."
Duke Mù said:
"I do not feel dishonored to ask you about the Dao,
but why do you answer me with frugality?"
What is the reason?"
Yóu Yú replied:
"I have heard that in the past, Yáo possessed the world,
eating from earthen bowls
and drinking from earthen pots.
His territory extended south to Jiāozhǐ,
north to Yōudū,
and east and west to where the sun and moon rise and set.
None failed to submit and be obedient.
Yáo chán (passed on) the empire,
Yú Shùn received it,
and made food vessels.
They cut down mountain trees to obtain materials,
smoothed and sawed to refine their form,
and applied black lacquer on them.
These were transported to the palace to be used as food vessels.
The feudal lords considered this increasingly extravagant,
and thirteen states did not submit.
Shùn chán (passed on) the empire and transmitted it to Yǔ.
Yǔ made sacrificial vessels.
He lacquered the outside in black,
and painted the inside in red.
A silk cloth was used as a cushion,
and a Jiang mat had patterned borders.
The cups and vessels were decorated with color,
and the wine vessels and trays had embellishments.
This was even more extravagant,
and thirty-three states did not submit.
After the Xià Hòu clan passed away,
the Yīn people received it.
They made a grand carriage,
and erected nine streamers.
Eating utensils are carved and adorned,
cups and goblets are engraved and inlaid,
white jade adorns the painted walls,
cushions and mats are decorated with intricate designs.
This is excessive luxury,
and yet the number of states that do not submit is fifty-three.
All the gentlemen understand elegant writing,
but the number of those who wish to submit becomes even fewer.
Therefore, your servant says:
"Frugality is the way."
Yóu Yú left,
and the Duke then summoned Nèishǐ Liào and told him,
saying:
"I have heard that a neighboring state with a sage is a cause for concern for a rival state.
Now Yóu Yú
is a sage.
I am worried about him.
What shall I do?"
Nèishǐ Liào said:
"I have heard that the dwelling of the Róng king
is remote and the roads are far,
and he has not heard the voices of the Central States.
Your Lordship should send him female musicians
to disrupt his government,
Then, he requested a date from Yóu Yú on my behalf,
in order to loosen his remonstrances.
When discord arises between that ruler and his ministers,
then we can plan against him."
The ruler said,
"Agreed."
Thereupon, he sent the Inner Scribe Liào
to present the Róng King with sixteen female musicians,
and took the opportunity to request a date from Yóu Yú.
The Róng King agreed,
saw the female musicians and was delighted by them,
setting up wine and spreading out drinks,
listening to music day after day,
and did not move his encampment for the entire year,
half of his cattle and horses died.
Yóu Yú returned,
and consequently remonstrated with the Róng King,
but the Róng King did not listen.
Therefore, Yóu Yú then left him and went to Qín.
Duke Mù of Qín welcomed him and appointed him as a senior minister with a bow,
asking about their military strength and their terrain.
Having obtained this information,
he raised troops and attacked them,
annexing twelve states
kāi dì qiān lǐ.
Thus it is said:
"Indulging in feminine pleasures,
and not attending to the affairs of state,
is the calamity of national ruin."
What is meant by "being estranged from the inner court and indulging in distant travels?"
In the past, Duke Jǐng of Qí (Qí Jǐng Gōng) traveled to the sea
and found pleasure in it.
He proclaimed to the high officials, saying:
"Whoever speaks of returning shall die."
Yán Zhuōjù said:
"If Your Lordship travels to the sea and finds pleasure in it,
what shall I do if someone plots against the state?
Even if Your Lordship finds pleasure in it,
how will you be at peace?"
Duke Jǐng of Qí (Qí Jǐng Gōng) said:
"I, your lord, issued a decree, saying,
'Whoever speaks of returning shall die.'
Now you violate my decree."
He raised his halberd to strike him.
Yán Zhuōjù said:
"In the past, Jié killed Guān Lóngféng
and Zhòu killed Prince Bǐgān.
Even if Your Lordship kills me,
"Using three is permissible.
My words are for the sake of the state,
not for my own sake."
He stretched his neck forward and said:
"The ruler will strike him!"
The ruler then put down his spear
and hastened to his chariot to return.
After three days,
he heard that the people of the state were plotting
not to let Duke Jǐng of Qí 齊景公 enter.
The reason Duke Jǐng of Qí 齊景公 was ultimately able to possess the state of Qí 齊 was
due to the strength of Yán Zhuōjù 顏涿聚.
Therefore it is said:
"Separating from the inner circle and wandering afar
is the way to endanger oneself."
What is meant by
"making mistakes and not listening to loyal ministers?"
Formerly, Duke Huán of Qí 齊桓公 assembled the feudal lords nine times,
rectified the world once,
and became the leader of the Five Hegemons,
with Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 assisting him.
When Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 grew old
and was no longer able to handle affairs,
he retired to his home.
Huán Gōng followed up and asked him, saying:
"Zhòngfǔ is at home sick,
if unfortunately he does not recover from this illness,
to whom should the government be transferred in peace?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"I am old,
it is not appropriate to ask me.
However,
I have heard it said,
'No one knows a minister better than his ruler,
no one knows a son better than his father.'
Your Lordship, try to decide it with your own heart."
The ruler said:
"What about Bào Shūyá?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"Not acceptable.
Bào Shūyá is a person who is
stubborn and arrogant towards superiors,
being stubborn, he oppresses the people with violence,
being obstinate, he cannot win the hearts of the people,
being arrogant, his subordinates will not work for him,
his heart knows no fear,
he is not an assistant for a hegemon."
The duke said:
"Then what about Shù Diāo?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"That won't do.
It is human nature that everyone loves their own body.
Your Grace is jealous and fond of the inner palace.
Shù Diāo castrated himself in order to manage the inner palace.
If he does not love his own body,
how can he love his lord?"
The Duke said:
"Then, what about Wèi Gōngzǐ Kāifāng?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"That won't do.
The distance between Qí and Wèi is no more than ten days' journey.
Kāifāng, in serving his lord,
desiring to please his lord,
for fifteen years did not return to see his parents.
This is not human nature.
If he is not close to his parents,
how can he be close to his lord?"
The Duke said:
"Then, what about Yì Yá?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"That won't do.
Yì Yá caters to his lord's taste.
The only thing his lord has not tasted is human flesh.
Yì Yá steamed his son's head and presented it,
which your lord knows.
Of human sentiments, none is without love for their child.
Now he steams his child to serve as food for you,
if he doesn't love his own child,
how then could he love you, my lord?"
The duke said,
"Then who is suitable?"
Guǎn Zhòng said,
"Xí Péng is suitable.
As a person,
he is firm within and incorruptible without,
with few desires and abundant trustworthiness.
Being firm within
is enough to set an example,
being incorruptible without
means he can bear great responsibility,
having few desires
means he can oversee the masses,
and abundant trustworthiness
means he can be close to neighboring states.
This is the assistant of a hegemon;
you should employ him, my lord."
The duke said,
"Nuò."
After living there for a year or so,
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 died.
The ruler then did not employ Xí Péng 隰朋
but instead employed Shù Diāo 豎刁.
Diāo 刁 was in charge of affairs for three years.
Duke Huán 桓公 traveled south to Tángfù 堂阜.
Shù Diāo 豎刁, along with Yì Yá 易牙,
the Wèi 衛 prince Kāifāng 開方, and high officials, started a rebellion.
Duke Huán 桓公 died of thirst and hunger in the chambers of the south gate.
The guards of the palace,
three months after his death, did not bury him,
and maggots crawled out of the door.
Therefore, Duke Huán's 桓公 army rampaged across the land,
and he became the leader of the Five Hegemons.
In the end, he was assassinated by his ministers
and his great name was destroyed.
He became a laughingstock to the world.
Why was this?
It was because he didn't listen to Guǎn Zhòng 管仲.
Therefore, it is said:
"To err and not listen to loyal subjects,
to act solely on one's own will,
then one destroys one's great name
and it is the beginning of being laughed at by others."
What is meant by "not assessing one's own strength"?
In the past, when Qín attacked Yíyáng,
the Hàn clan was anxious.
Gōngzhòng Péng said to the ruler of Hàn:
"Other states are not to be relied upon;
how about using Zhāng Yí to make peace with Qín?
Use bribes of famous cities
and join them in attacking Chǔ to the south.
This would resolve the trouble with Qín
and create harm with Chǔ."
The ruler said:
"Good."
He then prepared Gōngzhòng's journey,
intending to make peace with Qín to the west.
The King of Chǔ heard of this,
and became afraid.
He summoned Chén Zhěn and told him, saying:
"Hán Péng is about to make peace with Qín to the west.
What shall we do now?"
Chén Zhěn said:
"If Qín obtains one capital city from Hàn,
and mobilizes its well-trained soldiers,
then Qín and Hàn will unite to advance south towards Chǔ.
This is what the King of Qín sacrifices to his ancestors in the temple to pray for;
the harm to Chǔ will certainly be great.
Your Majesty should quickly dispatch a trusted minister,
increase the number of carriages,
and increase the value of the gifts,
to present to Hàn, saying:
To listen to the empty words of Chǔ
and belittle the real disaster of the powerful Qín is
the basis for endangering the state."
The ruler of Hán did not listen.
Gōngzhòng became angry and retired,
not attending court for ten days.
Yíyáng became increasingly urgent,
the ruler of Hán ordered messengers to urge soldiers from Chǔ,
carriages and canopies followed one another
but no soldiers arrived.
Yíyáng was indeed captured,
becoming a laughingstock among the lords.
Therefore it is said:
"If one does not assess their own strength internally
and relies on the lords externally,
then the danger of the state being weakened is at hand."
What does it mean for a small state to be without propriety?
In the past, the Jìn prince Chóng'ěr fled his country,
passing through Cáo,
the ruler of Cáo bared his upper body to watch him.
Lí Fùjī and Shū Zhān attended before him.
Shū Zhān said to the ruler of Cáo:
"I observe the Jìn prince,
he is no ordinary man.
If you treat him without propriety,
if he one day returns to his country and raises troops,
I fear that it will harm Cáo.
You would be better off killing him."
Then it is a situation of unparalleled power.
Solitary Indignation, Chapter Eleven.
Men of wisdom and strategy
must have far-reaching vision and be discerning.
If not discerning,
they cannot expose private wrongdoings.
Men capable of upholding the law
must be strong, resolute, and upright.
If not upright,
they cannot correct deceit.
A subject who follows orders and performs his duties,
and manages his office according to the law,
is not what is meant by a powerful minister.
What is meant by a powerful minister
is one who acts on his own without orders,
violates the law to benefit himself,
diminishes the state to enrich his family,
and is able to control his ruler.
This is what is meant by a powerful minister.
If men of wisdom and strategy are discerning
and heeded,
they will expose the secret behaviors of powerful ministers.
If men capable of upholding the law are upright
and heeded,
they will correct the deceitful actions of powerful ministers.
Therefore, if those skilled in wisdom, techniques, and law are employed,
then highly esteemed ministers will inevitably be outside the bounds of the law.
Thus, those skilled in wisdom and law and the powerful officials are
enemies who cannot coexist.
If the powerful officials monopolize important matters,
then both the outer and inner circles will be at their disposal.
Therefore, if feudal lords are not relied upon,
then affairs will not be handled appropriately,
hence rival states will speak well of them.
If the various officials are not relied upon,
then their careers will not advance,
hence the assembled ministers will be at their disposal.
If the imperial attendants are not relied upon,

Therefore, the sage
Examining the reality of right and wrong,
observing the circumstances of order and chaos.
Therefore, in governing the state,

showing compassion for the common people and light punishments
What the people delight in,

Occupying a position that deviates from the Way,

Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng's 楚莊王 younger brother, Chūn Shēn Jūn 春申君,

Chūn Shēn Jūn's 春申君's principal wife was named Jiǎ 甲.
Yú 余 wanted the lord to abandon his wife,

"To be able to be the lord's concubine
I am truly fortunate.

The situation makes it impossible to serve both together.
Rather than die at the hands of the wife,

The lord then believed concubine Yú's deception,

Yú then wanted to kill Jiǎ

The ruler was angry

Therefore, the wife was falsely abandoned as a concubine because of me,

Judging from this,

The relationship between a ruler and his ministers

How strange then that the wise and virtuous are put to death!
This is why Shāng Qūn 商君 was torn apart by chariots in Qín 秦,

Generally, ministers,

Therefore, those with skill and strategy in serving others

Only an enlightened ruler can understand this.
The scholars of the world, when advising rulers,

The rulers of the world admire the name of benevolence and righteousness

Therefore, in serious cases, the state is destroyed and the ruler dies;

How can this be shown?
To give to the poor and needy,

If one gives to the poor and needy,

If the state has those without merit receiving rewards,

They do not urgently encourage vigorous farming and rapid production internally;

Therefore, treacherous and self-serving ministers become more numerous,

What else are we waiting for but destruction?
Now, severe punishments are what the people fear;

Heavy penalties are what the people detest.
this is what the people abhor.
Therefore, the sage
displays what they fear

From this, I understand that benevolence, righteousness, love, and kindness are insufficient for use,
while severe punishments and heavy penalties are what can govern a state.
Without the authority of the whip and spur,

wú wēi yán zhī shì, [Without the aura of authority,]

chéng zhōu zhī ān, [The safety of riding in boats,]

Governing a state with effective methods of reward and punishment
is like traveling on land with a sturdy carriage and fine horses,
or navigating on water with a light boat and convenient oars.
Those who use them can then achieve their goals.
Yī Yǐn obtained them,

Guǎn Zhòng obtained them,

Shāng Jūn obtained them,

These three men
were all clear about the methods of hegemony and kingship,

they appropriately met the intentions of enlightened rulers of their time.
Thus, there were commoners who were directly appointed
to positions as high ministers and prime ministers;
holding positions and governing the state,
they had the reality of honoring the ruler and expanding the territory;

Tāng obtained Yī Yǐn,

Duke Huán obtained Guǎn Zhòng,
and became the leader of the Five Hegemons,
To unite the feudal lords nine times

Xiàogōng (孝公) obtaining Shāng Jūn (商君)

Therefore, having loyal ministers

As for Yù Ràng (豫讓) being a minister of Zhì Bó (智伯),

When Xiāngzǐ (襄子) killed Zhì Bó (智伯),

Although he endured self-mutilation and death

whatsoever.
This is what I would demote,
yet the rulers of the world consider them loyal and elevate them.
In ancient times, there were Bó Yí 伯夷 and Shū Qí 叔齊,
King Wǔ 武王 offered them the empire, but they refused it.
The two men starved to death at the mausoleum of Shǒu Yáng 首陽.
Such ministers
fear no heavy punishment,
desire no great rewards,
they cannot be controlled by penalties,
they cannot be commanded by rewards.
These are called useless ministers.
What I lack and would dismiss,
is what the rulers of the world have many of and seek.
A proverb says:

This is disrespectful speech.
However,
ancient proverbs are never without basis,

This refers to rulers who are robbed, killed, and die.
If a ruler has no methods or techniques

shàn shì zhǔ duàn,

And they fear that the fathers, elder brothers, and heroic figures

Therefore, the "Spring and Autumn Annals" records it, saying:

Things seen recently:
Lǐ Duì, in his employment by Zhào,

Chapter Fifteen: Signs of Ruin
Generally, when a ruler's state is small while his family's wealth is great,
and his authority is weak while his ministers' power is strong,
he is liable to ruin.
If he simplifies laws and prohibitions
but is preoccupied with schemes and strategems,
neglects internal affairs
and relies on external alliances,
he is liable to ruin.
If ministers pursue learning,
disciples love argumentation,
merchants accumulate wealth abroad,
and the common people value weapons,
he is liable to ruin.
If he indulges in palaces, pavilions, terraces, and ponds,
engages in elaborate carriages, clothing, and playthings,
loves to exhaust and expose the common people,
and squanders wealth and resources,
he is liable to ruin.
If he observes auspicious days,
serves ghosts and spirits,
believes in divination,
and loves sacrifices,
he is liable to ruin.
A state that
elevates people based on hearsay without verification,
is doomed to perish.
A state where official positions can be obtained through relentless seeking,
and noble titles and stipends can be bought with wealth,
is doomed to perish.
A state whose leaders are leisurely and accomplish nothing,
are indecisive and make few decisions,
have unclear likes and dislikes,
and establish no firm policies,
is doomed to perish.
A state whose leaders are gluttonous and insatiable,
are short-sighted and love petty gains,
is doomed to perish.
A state that delights in seductive words that are not in accordance with the law,
enjoys eloquent arguments but does not seek their practical application,
and indulges in ornate writing without regard for its usefulness,
is doomed to perish.
A state whose leaders are shallow and easily understood,
leak secrets and keep nothing hidden,
are unable to be discreet,
and divulge the conversations of all their ministers,
is doomed to perish.
A state whose leaders are stubborn and inflexible,
reject advice and love to win arguments,
Those who disregard the state
and lightly rely on their own confidence
are liable to perish.
Those who rely on foreign alliances
and neglect their close neighbors,
who depend on the rescue of the powerful,
and scorn the country they oppress,
are liable to perish.
Those who have foreign travelers and sojourners,
who lavish funds abroad,
whose superiors are distracted by schemes,
and whose inferiors are engaged in popular affairs,
are liable to perish.
If the people trust their prime minister,
if subordinates are incapable of surpassing their superiors,
and if the ruler loves and trusts him but cannot depose him,
they are liable to perish.
Those who do not employ the talented within their borders
but seek to ennoble scholars from abroad,
who do not evaluate and test based on merit and achievements,
but instead favor promoting and appointing based on reputation,
and allow foreign travelers to rise in nobility and override established norms,
are liable to perish.
To lightly esteem what is correct,
and for the sons of concubines to claim equality;
when the heir apparent is not yet decided and the ruler passes away,
the state can be destroyed.
To be arrogant and without remorse,
for the state to be in chaos yet boast of its successes,
to not assess the resources within the borders
and lightly antagonize its neighbors,
the state can be destroyed.
For a small state to not occupy a humble position,
to have little strength yet not fear the powerful,
to be without courtesy and insult great neighbors,
to be greedy, stubborn, and clumsy in diplomacy,
the state can be destroyed.
When an heir apparent has already been designated,
and a consort is taken from a powerful enemy as a new wife,
then the heir apparent is in danger,
if this is so, then the ministers will easily change their minds;
when ministers easily change their minds,
the state can be destroyed.
To be fearful and timid in defense,
to have early insight but a soft and weak heart,
to know that something is advisable,
but to decide yet not dare to act on it,
the state can be destroyed.
If the ruler is abroad and the state is reorganized,
if the hostage prince has not returned
and the ruler changes his heir,
then the state will be in disarray;
a state in disarray
can be destroyed.
To humiliate and insult great ministers and be intimate with those close to him,
to punish and kill the common people and go against their envoys,
those who harbor anger and think of shame
and specialize in learning will become rebels;
those where rebels arise
can be destroyed.
If great ministers are powerful and influential on both sides,
if fathers and elder brothers are many and strong,
and there are internal factions and external support to contend for power,
the state can be destroyed.
If the words of maids and concubines are heeded,
if the wisdom of those who indulge in pleasures is employed,
if there is sorrow and lamentation both within and without
and illegal acts are frequently committed,
the state can be destroyed.
To treat great ministers with disdain and contempt,
to show no respect to fathers and elder brothers,
to exhaust the people with labor,
Those who kill the innocent
are liable to perish.
Those who like to use cleverness to distort the law,
and frequently mix personal actions with public affairs,
whose laws and prohibitions are changed easily,
and whose orders are frequently issued,
are liable to perish.
Those who have no secure territory,
whose city walls are dilapidated,
who have no stores,
whose wealth is meager,
who have no defenses for defense and war,
and who lightly engage in attacks and conquests,
are liable to perish.
Those whose lineage is not long-lived,
whose rulers frequently die young,
whose ruler is an infant,
whose high ministers hold all the power,
who cultivate alliances with foreigners to form factions,
and who frequently cede territory to secure alliances,
are liable to perish.
Those whose crown prince is honored and prominent,
whose followers are numerous and strong,
who have many alliances with great states,
Those who prematurely display power and authority,
are liable to perish.
Those who are narrow-minded and impatient,
hasty and easily provoked,
whose minds are full of resentment and who do not consider the consequences,
are liable to perish.
A ruler who is often angry and fond of using military force,
who neglects fundamental teachings and values offensive warfare,
is liable to perish.
When noble ministers are jealous of each other,
great ministers become exceedingly powerful,
relying on enemy states for support from the outside,
while internally oppressing the common people,
attacking enemies to satisfy personal grudges,
and the ruler does not punish them,
the state is liable to perish.
If the ruler is unworthy but the concubine is wise,
the heir apparent is weak but the son of a secondary wife is strong-willed,
the officials are weak but the people are rebellious,
then the state is restless;
a restless state,
is liable to perish.
To harbor resentment without expressing it,
to suspend punishment without executing it,
If [the ruler] causes the assembled ministers to secretly resent [him]
and to become increasingly worried and fearful,
and [the future] remains unknowable for a long time,
[the state] is liable to perish.
If the command of the army and appointment of generals is too significant,
if the responsibility of border defense is too respected,
if [someone] exercises absolute authority and issues commands on their own,
acting independently without seeking permission,
[the state] is liable to perish.
If the queen is lewd and promiscuous,
if the principal mother keeps filth,
if there is indiscriminate mingling between the outer and inner quarters,
if there is no distinction between men and women,
this is called having "two rulers."
Having "two rulers"
means [the state] is liable to perish.
If the queen is of low status while the concubines are of high status,
if the crown prince is looked down upon while the sons of concubines are honored,
if the prime minister's chamber is treated lightly while the reception hall is valued,
such a situation leads to discord between the inner and outer [quarters of the court].
If there is discord between the inner and outer [quarters],
[the state] is liable to perish.
If senior ministers are extremely honored,
if factions and partisan groups are numerous and powerful,
If obstructions prevail, the ruler is cut off
and powerful ministers independently control the state,
that state is likely to perish.
If private cliques are employed in official positions,
if the hereditary privileges of the Mǎ Fǔ 馬府 family are abolished,
if local worthies are promoted based on local recommendations,
if diligent performance in official duties is disregarded,
if private conduct is valued and public service is disdained,
that state is likely to perish.
If the state treasury is empty while powerful ministers are wealthy,
if the registered households are poor while transient residents are rich,
if farmers and soldiers are impoverished,
if artisans and merchants profit,
that state is likely to perish.
If one sees great profit but does not pursue it,
if one hears of impending disaster but does not prepare for it,
if one is superficial in matters of defense,
and focuses on adorning oneself with benevolence and righteousness,
that state is likely to perish.
If one does not practice the filial piety appropriate for a ruler,
but admires the filial piety of commoners,
if one disregards the interests of the state,
and listens to the commands of the queen mother,
if women control the state,
Those who have suffered corporal punishment and are employed in positions of authority,
can bring about ruin.
Those who are skilled in argument but do not follow the law,
who are intelligent but lack strategic skill,
and rulers who are multi-talented
but do not conduct affairs according to legal standards,
can bring about ruin.
When close ministers advance and old friends retreat,
when the unworthy are employed and the virtuous and good are in hiding,
when those without merit are honored and the hardworking are despised,
in such cases, the people below resent it.
When the people below resent it,
this can bring about ruin.
When fathers, elder brothers, and great ministers receive emoluments and ranks that exceed their merit,
when ceremonial robes encroach upon established status,
when palaces and provisions are extravagantly lavish,
and the ruler does not prohibit this,
then the desires of the ministers will know no bounds.
When the desires of the ministers know no bounds,
this can bring about ruin.
When sons-in-law and grandsons of the nobility live in the same neighborhoods as the common people
and violently insult their neighbors,
this can bring about ruin.
Signs of Ruin
do not necessarily mean that ruin is inevitable,
but rather that ruin is possible.
Even two Yáos cannot both be kings,
and two Jiés cannot both bring about ruin.
The mechanism of ruin or kingship
lies in whether there is order or chaos,
and the balance of strength and weakness between the two.
A tree breaks because it is riddled with decay,
and a wall crumbles because it is full of cracks.
However, even if a tree is decayed,
it will not break without a strong wind;
even if a wall is cracked,
it will not crumble without heavy rain.
If the ruler of a myriad chariots
is able to employ methods and enforce laws,
and sees the wind and rain as the signs of ruin in his prince,
conquering the world will not be difficult for him.
Three Safeguards, Chapter Sixteen
A ruler has three safeguards.
If the three safeguards are complete,
the state is secure and the person is honored;
if the three safeguards are incomplete,
the state is in danger and the person is in peril.
What are the three safeguards?
When a subject discusses the errors of those in power,
the faults of those in office,
and the feelings of the people,
if the ruler does not keep this information to himself
but reveals it to his close associates and capable men,
Regarding high officials,
those who act in such a way are encroaching.
This is called "the three defenses not complete."
If the three defenses are not complete,
then it is a sign of robbery and murder.
Generally, there are three kinds of robbery:
There is overt robbery,
there is robbery through affairs,
and there is robbery through punishment.
A subject who possesses the high status of a great minister [dà chén]
controls the important affairs of the state externally to enrich his followers,
so that external and internal matters
cannot be carried out without his approval.
Even if there are worthy and virtuous people,
those who oppose him will certainly suffer misfortune,
and those who obey him will certainly have good fortune.
In that case, none of the officials will dare to be loyal to the ruler and concerned about the country
to strive for the benefit of the state.
Even if the ruler is wise and virtuous,
he cannot make decisions alone,
and if the officials dare not be loyal to the ruler,
then the state will become a doomed state.
This is called "the state has no ministers."
If a state has no capable ministers,
does it merely mean that the Lángzhōng (郎中, Palace Attendants) positions are vacant
or that the number of court officials is small?
When the multitude of ministers hold onto their stipends to nurture their own connections,
pursue private interests instead of demonstrating public loyalty,
this is called "obvious robbery" (míng jié 明劫).
They sell favors and monopolize power,
using external influence to overcome internal affairs,
speaking insidiously about the forms of fortune, misfortune, gain, and loss,
in order to cater to the ruler's likes and dislikes.
If the ruler listens to them,
lowering himself and belittling the state to enrich them,
when affairs fail, they share the blame with the ruler,
but when achievements are made, the ministers alone claim the credit.
When all those in positions of power
unanimously agree and speak in unison to praise their merits,
then the ruler will certainly not believe those who speak ill of them;
this is called "affairs robbery" (shì jié 事劫).
As for guarding and managing prisons,
and controlling punishments and penalties,
when ministers monopolize these,
this is called "punishment robbery" (xíng jié 刑劫).
If the three guards (sān shǒu 三守) are not complete,
Then the three usurpations arise;
when the three safeguards are complete,
then the three usurpations cease.
When the three usurpations are stopped and blocked,
then you will be a true king.
Chapter Seventeen: Provisions Within
The sovereign's trouble lies in trusting people;
trust people,

The relationship between a minister and his ruler

Husband and wife

A saying goes:

Thus, if they act in the opposite way,

A husband at fifty

When a woman of declining beauty serves a husband who loves sensual pleasures,
Then one finds oneself neglected and demeaned,

This is why empresses and

Therefore, the *Táo Zuǒ Chūnqiū* says:

If the ruler does not know this,

Therefore, it is said:
if many people benefit from the ruler's death,

Therefore, Wáng Liáng loved horses,

A skilled doctor willingly sucks the wounds of others

The emotion is not hating people,

Therefore, the parties of Empresses,

The emotion is not hating the ruler,

Thus, when halos appear around the sun or moon,

Beware of those who are hated;

Therefore, the enlightened ruler [míng wáng] does not engage in unverified and unexamined matters,

Do not eat extraordinary food.
Listen from afar, and observe up close

examine words that are the same and different

occasionally verify with fivefold (groupings)

Hold onto the latter to respond to the former,
follow the law to govern the masses,
observe all matters for comparison.
If officials receive no undeserved rewards,

if executions are always just,

If corvée labor is excessive, then the people will suffer;

Oppressing the people to enrich the nobles,

Therefore it is said:
If corvée labor is light, then the people will be at peace;

Now, that water overcomes fire is also clear;

Now, the prohibition of wickedness in governance is even clearer than this;

Ancient traditions say,

Yet, the laws and ordinances that are prepared,

Great ministers form factions,

In secret they praise each other, while openly they disparage each other,

If the ruler is closed off and obscured,

Facing South, Number Eighteen.
The ruler's error

Now, the people whom he uses to guard against the others,

If the ruler cannot clarify the laws

If a ruler abandons the law and uses his ministers to control other ministers,

When praise and criticism are intertwined,

Ministers,

if they do not disregard the law and act with autonomy,

if they do not feign loyalty and trustworthiness,

These three

If a ruler commands his ministers,

even if they have virtuous conduct,

even if they have loyalty and trustworthiness,

This is called understanding the law (míng fǎ).
A ruler can be misled by events or
blocked by words.
These two things must be observed.
Rén chén yì yán shì zhě,
seek little resources

If the ruler is tempted and does not investigate,

Such a case is called temptation;
those tempted by affairs are trapped by troubles.
If their advancement in speech is little,

Those who are not believed are guilty.
If those with meritorious affairs are not rewarded,

The way of the ruler

Even if affairs have merit,

If a minister is designing an affair for the ruler

Then they first utter a persuasive statement, saying:

He who is obstructed in speech is controlled by his ministers.
The way of the ruler

Words that have no beginning or end, and arguments that have no way to be verified,

Those who avoid responsibility by not speaking

When the ruler causes his ministers to speak,

Then no subject would dare to speak recklessly,

If the ruler wants to accomplish something,

Those who understand this,
rely on reason and abandon desires.
There is a proper way to undertake things:

A deluded ruler is not like this;

Even if the expenditure is double the income,

Such a situation means the achievement is small

Generally speaking, an accomplishment
is when the income is great
If its output is small,

Small merit will be achieved,

Those who do not understand governance

Change or not change,

If the people are foolish and do not know disorder,

The ruler,
if wise, can know governance,

The explanation lies in
Shāng Jūn’s use of inner and outer iron-tipped spears,

Therefore, foolish, stupid, lazy, and decadent people

Therefore, Yín Hǔ was subjected to slander.
If one changes a small thing and loses a great advantage,

Divining with tortoise shells and counting milfoil stalks,

Divining with tortoise shells and counting milfoil stalks,

Jù Xīn served Yān,

"Great Fortune,"

Abandoning laws

Jīng Gōng Wáng of Jīng (荊恭王) and Jìn Lì Gōng of Jìn (晉厲公) fought at Yānlíng (鄢陵),

There is public righteousness.
