Thus, the common man desired jade,
while Zǐ Hǎn did not desire jade.
Therefore it is said:
"Desiring non-desire,
and not valuing hard-to-obtain goods."
Wáng Shòu was carrying books and walking,
and saw Xú Féng on the road in Zhōu.
Féng said:
"Affairs
Action is
born from the times,
and the wise have no constant affairs.
Writings are
words,
words are born from knowledge,
and the wise do not hoard books.
Now why do you alone carry them and walk?"
Thereupon, Wáng Shòu burned his books and danced with them.
Therefore, the wise do not teach with words and discourse,
and the intelligent do not use book chests to store books.
This is what the world errs in,
and Wáng Shòu repeats it,
which is learning what is not to be learned.
Therefore, it is said:
"Learning what is not to be learned
is returning to the errors of the masses."
Now, things have a constant form,
and one should follow and guide them.
Following the form of things,
therefore, in stillness, one builds upon virtue,
and in movement, one follows the Dao.
There was a man of Sòng who made artificial mulberry leaves for his ruler out of ivory,
and it took him three years to complete them.
The flourishing and withering of stems and branches,
the minute hairs and abundant luster,
mixed among the chǔ (paper mulberry) leaves,
cannot be distinguished.
This person then received salary and rank in the state of Sòng based on his skill.
Lièzǐ heard of this and said:
"If heaven and earth took three years to produce a single leaf,
then things that have leaves would be few."
Therefore, not to rely on the resources of heaven and earth
but to load it onto one person's body,
not to follow the principles of natural order
but to learn one person's wisdom,
these are all one-leaf actions.
Therefore, the crops of winter plowing,
even Hòujì could not admire them;
in a bountiful year of great harvests,
even Zāng Huò could not dislike them.
Relying on one person's strength,
then Hòujì is insufficient;
following nature,
then Zāng Huò has excess.
Therefore, it is said:
"Rely on the naturalness of all things
and dare not interfere."
The orifices are
the windows and doors of spirit and intelligence.
Ears and eyes are exhausted by sounds and sights,
spirit is exhausted by outward appearances,
therefore, the center has no master.
When the center has no master,
then even if misfortune and fortune are like hills and mountains,
there is no way to recognize them.
Therefore, it is said:
"Without going out the door,
one can know the world;
without peeking through the window,
one can know the Dao of Heaven."
This says that spirit and intelligence do not depart from their true nature.
Lord Xiang of Zhao learned charioteering from Prince Yuqi.
Soon after, he raced Yuqi,
changed horses three times, and each time lagged behind.
Lord Xiang said:
"Your teaching of charioteering has not exhausted the technique?"
Yuqi replied:
"The technique is exhausted,
but its application is excessive.
Generally, what is valued in charioteering is that
the horse's body is secure in the chariot,
the human mind is harmonized with the horse,
Only then can one advance swiftly and reach far.
Now, if Your Lordship lags behind, you wish to catch up with me;
but if you go first, you fear being overtaken by me.
Now, in leading the way and striving for distance,
it's either being first or being last;
yet whether you are first or last, your mind is entirely on me.
How then can Your Lordship control the horses?
This is why Your Lordship falls behind."
Bái Gōng Shèng, agitated with worry,
dismissed the court.
He held his staff upside down and the sharp end pierced his forehead,
blood flowed to the ground, yet he did not realize it.
The people of Zhèng heard of it and said:
"If he forgets his forehead,
what will he not forget?"
Therefore, it is said:
"The farther one goes out,
the less one knows."
This means that if one's wisdom encompasses what is far,
then what is left behind is what is near.
Therefore, the sage has no constant course of action.
He can combine wisdom,
therefore it is said:
"He knows without acting."
Being able to oversee everything together,
therefore it is said:
"To be enlightened without seeing."
Acting according to the times to carry out affairs,
achieving merits by relying on resources,
using the abilities of all things
and gaining profit on top of that,
therefore it is said:
"To accomplish without acting."
For three years after King Zhuāng of Chǔ ascended to the throne,
no orders were issued,
and no government actions were taken.
The Right Sīmǎ took his seat
and spoke to the King in a veiled manner, saying:
"There is a bird perched on a hill in the south,
for three years it does not spread its wings,
it does not fly or sing,
silently without a sound.
What is this called?"
The King said:
"For three years it does not spread its wings,
it is about to grow its feathers;
it does not fly or sing,
it is about to observe the laws of the people.
Although it does not fly,
When it flies, it must soar to the sky;
although it does not cry,
when it cries, it will surely astonish people.
You may step aside,
I, the unworthy one, understand it now."
After half a year,
he then personally took charge of the government.
He dismissed ten officials,
promoted nine,
executed five senior ministers,
and appointed six hermits,
and the state became greatly ordered.
He raised an army to attack Qí,
defeating them at Xúzhōu,
defeating Jìn at Héyōng,
gathering the feudal lords at Sòng,
and thus he became the hegemon of the world.
King Zhuāng of Chǔ did not concern himself with minor benefits,
therefore he achieved great renown;
he did not reveal his intentions early,
therefore he achieved great accomplishments.
Therefore, it is said:
"Great vessels are completed late;
great sounds are rarely heard."
Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng 楚莊王 wanted to attack Yuè 越.
Dù Zǐ 杜子 remonstrated, saying:
"Your Majesty's attack on Yuè 越,
what is the reason for it?"
The king said:
"Their government is chaotic and their army is weak."
Dù Zǐ 杜子 said:
"Your subject is foolish and worries about [the limitations of]
wisdom. It is like the eye,
it can see things a hundred steps away,
but it cannot see its own eyelashes.
Your Majesty's army was defeated by Qín 秦 and Jìn 晉,
losing territory of several hundred *lǐ* 里,
this is the weakness of the army.
Zhuāng Xī Qiāo 莊蹊蹻 acts as a bandit within your territory
but the officials cannot stop him,
this is the chaos of the government.
Your Majesty's weakness and chaos
are no less than that of Yuè 越,
yet you wish to attack Yuè 越,
this is wisdom like the eye."
The king then stopped [his plan].
Therefore, knowing is difficult,
it is not in seeing others,
but in seeing oneself.
Therefore, it is said:
"To see oneself is called clear-sightedness."
Zǐ Xià 子夏 saw Zēng Zǐ 曾子.
Zēng Zǐ 曾子 said:
"Why are you so plump?"
He replied:
"I won a battle,
therefore I am plump."
Zēng Zǐ 曾子 said:
"What do you mean?"
Zǐ Xià 子夏 said:
"When I went in and saw the righteousness of the former kings,
I esteemed it;
when I went out and saw the pleasure of wealth and nobility,
I also esteemed it.
The two battled in my heart,
and not knowing which would win or lose,
therefore I was thin.
Now the righteousness of the former kings has won,
therefore I am plump."
Therefore, the difficulty of having a will (志, zhì) lies not in overcoming others,
but in overcoming oneself.
Therefore, it is said:
"To overcome oneself is called strength."
The Zhōu dynasty had a jade tablet.
Zhòu (紂) ordered Jiāo Gé (膠鬲) to obtain it,
but King Wén (文王) did not give it to him.
Fèi Zhòng (費仲) came to ask for it,
and King Wén gave it to him.
This shows that Jiāo Gé was virtuous
while Fèi Zhòng was unprincipled.
Zhōu (周) disliked virtuous men succeeding,
therefore he gave it to Fèi Zhòng.
King Wén’s promotion of Tài Gōng (太公) on the banks of the Wèi River
was to honor him;
but to entrust the jade tablet to Fèi Zhòng
was to show his affection.
Therefore, it is said:
"If one does not respect one's teacher,
and does not value one's resources,
even if one understands, one is greatly misguided;
this is called essential subtlety."
Discourse (Shuō Lín) 22
Tāng (湯) was about to attack Jié (桀),
but feared that the world would accuse him of greed.
Therefore, he offered the throne to Wù Guāng (務光).
Fearing that Wù Guāng would accept,
he sent someone to persuade Wù Guāng, saying:
"Tāng killed the ruler and wants to pass on a bad reputation to you,
Therefore, he yielded the throne to his son."
Wù Guāng (務光) then threw himself into the river.
King Wǔ of Qín (秦武王) ordered Gān Mào (甘茂) to choose what he desired to be
in service or in action,
Mèng Mǎo (孟卯) said:
"It would be better for you to be a servant.
Your strength lies
in being an envoy.
Even if you are a servant,
the king will still employ you in the same way.
If you wear the servant's seal while engaging in affairs,
it is akin to holding multiple offices."
Zǐ Yǔ (子圉) met Confucius at the residence of the Grand Steward of Shāng (商太宰).
Confucius left,
Zǐ Yǔ (子圉) entered
and asked about the guest.
The Grand Steward said:
"Having seen Confucius,
I regard you as insignificant as a flea.
I will now present him to the ruler."
Zǐ Yǔ (子圉), fearing that Confucius would become more influential than him with the ruler,
then said to the Grand Steward:
"If the ruler has already met Confucius,
he will also regard you as a flea."
Consequently, the Grand Steward never saw him again.
Wèi Huì Wáng made the alliance at Jiùlǐ,
and was about to be re-established by the Son of Heaven.
Péng Xǐ said to the ruler of Zhèng:
"Your Lordship, do not listen to him.
Great states dislike having a Son of Heaven,
small states benefit from it.
If Your Lordship and the great states do not listen,
how can Wèi be able to establish him with the small states?"
The people of Jìn attacked Xíng,
and Qí Huán Gōng was about to rescue it.
Bào Shū said:
"It is too early.
If Xíng does not perish,
Jìn will not be exhausted;
if Jìn is not exhausted,
Qí will not be respected.
Moreover, the merit of supporting the precarious
is not as great as the virtue of preserving the perished.
Your Lordship would do better to rescue it late, so as to exhaust Jìn,
then Qí will truly benefit.
Wait until Xíng perishes and then restore it,
and your reputation and reality will both be beautiful."
Huán Gōng therefore did not rescue it.
Zǐ Xū fled and was captured by a border guard.
Biān Hòu obtained it.
Zǐ Xū said:
"The ruler seeks me
because I possess a beautiful pearl.
Now, I have already lost it.
I will simply say:
'You, sir, took and swallowed it.'"
Thereupon, Hòu released him.
Qìng Fēng caused turmoil in Qí and desired to flee to Yuè.
His kinsman said:
"Jìn is near,
why not go to Jìn?"
Qìng Fēng said:
"Yuè is far,
advantageous for escaping calamity."
His kinsman said:
"If you change your disposition,
residing in Jìn would be acceptable;
if you do not change your disposition,
even though Yuè is far,
how can you find peace?"
Zhì Bó demanded land from Wèi Xuānzǐ,
Wèi Xuānzǐ did not grant it.
Rèn Zhāng said:
"Why not grant it?"
Xuān Zǐ said:
"To request land without a reason,
I therefore did not grant it."
Rèn Zhāng said:
"To demand land without a reason,
neighboring states will surely fear.
If he has heavy desires without satisfaction,
the world will surely be afraid.
If Your Lordship grants him the land,
Zhì Bó will surely become arrogant and underestimate his enemies,
neighboring states will surely fear and become close to each other.
Using the forces of those who are close to each other to face a state that underestimates its enemies,
then Zhì Bó's fate will not be long.
The *Book of Zhou* says:
'If you want to defeat someone,
you must first assist them;
if you want to take from someone,
you must first give to them.'
Your Lordship is better off giving to him in order to make Zhì Bó arrogant.
Moreover, why should Your Lordship abandon using the world to plot against the Zhì clan,
and instead only use our state as a hostage for the Zhì clan?"
The Lord said:
"Good."
Thereupon he gave him a city of ten thousand households.
Zhì Bó was greatly pleased,
Yīn suǒ dì yú Zhào,
they did not give it;
therefore he besieged Jìnyáng.
With Hán and Wèi rebelling from the outside,
and the Zhào clan responding from the inside,
the Zhì clan perished.
Duke Kāng of Qín built a terrace for three years.
The people of Jīng raised an army,
intending to use the army to attack Qí.
Rén Wàng said:
"Famine summons soldiers,
disease summons soldiers,
exhaustion summons soldiers,
disorder summons soldiers.
Your Lordship has been building a terrace for three years,
now the people of Jīng have raised an army and are about to attack Qí,
I fear that their attacking Qí is a feint,
and attacking Qín is the reality,
it would be better to prepare for it."
They garrisoned the eastern border,
and the people of Jīng stopped their advance.
Qí attacked Sòng,
and Sòng sent Zāngsūn Zǐ Nán to seek help from Jīng.
Jīng was very pleased,
Xǔ Jiù greatly urged him to send aid.
shèn quàn.
Zāng Sūnzǐ returned with worry.
His charioteer said:
"You sought aid and received it,
now you have a worried look,
why is that?"
Zāng Sūnzǐ said:
"Sòng is small and Qí is large.
To save small Sòng and offend large Qí,
this is what people worry about;
and the King of Jīng is pleased,
he will certainly consider me steadfast.
If I am steadfast and Qí is exhausted,
this is what benefits Jīng."
Zāng Sūnzǐ then returned.
The people of Qí captured five cities from Sòng,
but aid from Jīng did not arrive.
Marquis Wén of Wèi requested passage through Zhào
in order to attack Zhōngshān,
Marquis Sù of Zhào was about to deny it.
Zhào Kè said:
"Your Lordship is mistaken.
If Wèi attacks Zhōngshān but cannot take it,
then Wèi will certainly be exhausted.
If they withdraw, Wei will be weakened,
if Wei is weakened, Zhao will be strengthened.
If Wei captures Zhongshan,
they certainly cannot bypass Zhao to possess Zhongshan.
Those who are using troops
are Wei;
but those who will gain land
are Zhao.
Your Lordship must agree to it.
Agree to it and they will be greatly delighted,
they will know that Your Lordship benefits from it,
and they will certainly halt their campaign.
Your Lordship would be better off to lend them the road,
showing it as a matter of necessity."
Chī Yí Zǐpí served Tián Chéngzǐ.
Tián Chéngzǐ left Qi,
fled to Yan,
Chī Yí Zǐpí carried the documents and followed.
Reaching Wangyi,
Zǐpí said:
"Have you not heard of the snakes in the dried-up marsh?
When the marsh dries up,
the snakes will move.
A small snake said to a large snake:
'If you go and I follow you,
People thought snakes only moved by slithering,
and would surely kill their young.
"It would be better to bite each other and carry me so I can move,
then people will think of me as a divine lord!"
So they bit each other and carried
him across the main road.
People all avoided them,
saying:
"It's a divine lord!"
"Now, you are beautiful and I am ugly.
If people take you for my honored guest,
you would be a ruler of a thousand chariots;
if people take you for my envoy,
you would be a high minister of ten thousand chariots.
You would be better off being my attendant."
Tián Chéngzǐ then carried his baggage and followed him.
They arrived at an inn.
The innkeeper treated him with great respect
and offered wine and meat.
A man from Wēn
went to Zhōu, but Zhōu refused to take him in.
They asked him, saying:
"Are you a guest?"
He replied, saying:
"I am the master."
They asked the people of the lane about it, but no one knew.
Therefore, the officials imprisoned him.
The ruler sent someone to question him, saying:
"You are not a person of Zhōu 周,
yet you claim not to be a guest.
Why is this?"
He replied, saying:
"When I was young, I recited the *Shī* (Book of Poetry), which says:
'Under the whole heaven,
there is no land that is not the king's;
to the very borders of the land,
there is no one who is not the king's subject.'
Now, you, my ruler,
are the son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ 天子),
therefore I am a subject of the son of Heaven.
How can there be someone who is a subject of a person
and also a guest of that person?
Therefore, I said:
I am a master here."
The ruler ordered him to be released.
King Xuān of Hán 韓宣王 said to Jiū Liú 樛留:
"I wish to employ both Gōngzhòng 公仲 and Gōngshū 公叔 simultaneously.
Is that permissible?"
He replied, saying:
"It is not permissible.
The Jìn used the Six Ministers
and the state was divided.
Jiǎn Gōng used both Tián Chéng and Kàn Zhǐ
and Jiǎn Gōng was killed.
Wèi used both Xī Shǒu and Zhāng Yí,
and the territory west of the Yellow River was lost.
Now, if Your Majesty uses both,
those with great power will establish their factions,
and those with little power will borrow external authority.
If ministers have factions established within the court to be arrogant towards the ruler,
and have external alliances to partition territory,
then Your Majesty's state is in danger."
Shào Jì lost his fur coat because he was drunk and asleep.
The ruler of Sòng said:
"Is being drunk enough to lose a fur coat?"
He replied:
"Jíe lost the empire because of drunkenness,
and the "Kāng Gào" says
'Do not constantly indulge in wine,'
'constant wine' means habitual drinking.
Habitual drinking
causes the emperor to lose the empire,
and the commoner to lose his life."
Guǎn Zhòng and Xí Péng followed Duke Huán
to attack Gū Zhú.
When spring goes and winter returns,
one becomes bewildered and loses the way.
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 said:
"The wisdom of an old horse can be used."
So they released an old horse and followed it,
and consequently found the way.
Traveling in the mountains without water,
Xí Péng 隰朋 said:
"Ants dwell on the sunny side of the mountain in winter
and on the shady side of the mountain in summer.
For every inch of ant mound soil, there are eight feet of water."
So they dug the ground,
and consequently found water.
With the sagacity of Guǎn Zhòng 管仲
and the wisdom of Xí Péng 隰朋,
when they reached something they didn't know,
they didn't hesitate to learn from old horses and ants.
Now people, not knowing to use their foolish minds
to learn from the wisdom of the sages,
isn't that going too far?
Someone presented an immortality elixir to the King of Jīng 荊王,
and an announcer held it to enter (the palace).
A middle-ranking archer asked:
"Is it edible?"
(The announcer) said:
"Acceptable."
Therefore, he seized and ate it.
The king was greatly angered
and ordered someone to kill the archer.
The archer sent someone to speak to the king, saying:
"Your servant asked the gatekeeper,
and he said, 'It is edible.'
Therefore, your servant ate it.
Thus, your servant is not guilty,
but the blame lies with the gatekeeper.
Moreover, the guest presented a medicine of immortality.
If your servant eats it and the king kills your servant,
then it is a medicine of death.
This means the guest deceived the king.
To kill an innocent subject
and to reveal that someone deceived the king,
it is better to release your servant."
The king then did not kill him.
Tián Sì deceived the ruler of Zōu,
and the ruler of Zōu was about to have someone kill him.
Tián Sì was afraid
and told Huìzi.
Huìzi met with the ruler of Zōu and said:
"Now, if someone sees you,
and then pokes out one of their eyes,
Xī rú?"
The ruler said,
"I must kill him."
Huìzǐ said,
"A blind person,
both eyes being closed,
why do you not kill him?"
The ruler said,
"He cannot help but close them."
Huìzǐ said,
"Tián Sì behaved insolently towards the Marquis of Qí in the east,
and deceived the King of Jīng in the south.
Sì's deception of others
is like that of a blind person.
Why do you resent him?"
The ruler of Zōu then did not kill him.
Duke Mù of Lǔ caused many young masters
to seek officialdom in Jìn,
or to seek officialdom in Jīng.
Lí Chú said,
"To employ a person from Yuè to save a drowning child,
even though the people of Yuè are skilled swimmers,
the child will certainly not live.
To put out a fire by fetching water from the sea,
Although the sea has much water,
fire will certainly not be extinguished,
because distant water cannot put out a nearby fire.
Now, although Jìn 晉 and Jīng 荊 are strong,
Qí 齊 is nearby,
so is Lǔ 魯 worried that they cannot be saved?"
Yán Suí 嚴遂 did not like Zhōu Jūn 周君 and
worried about him.
Féng Jū 馮沮 said:
"Yán Suí 嚴遂 is chancellor,
and Hán Kuī 韓傀 is favored by the lord.
It would be better to send an assassin against Hán Kuī 韓傀,
then the lord will certainly think it was the Yán 嚴 family."
Zhāng Qiǎn 張譴, the chancellor of Hán 韓,
was sick and about to die.
Gōngchéng Wúzhèng 公乘無正, carrying thirty gold pieces,
inquired about his illness.
After a day,
the lord asked Zhāng Qiǎn 張譴, saying:
"If you die,
whom should I appoint to replace you?"
He replied:
"Wúzhèng 無正 values the law and fears his superiors.
However,
he is not as good as Gōngzǐ Shíwǒ 公子食我 in winning the people."
Zhāng Qiǎn 张谴 died because
he relied on the Xiàng Gōng 相公 chariot without being upright.
Yuè Yáng 乐羊, as a general of Wèi 魏, attacked Zhōngshān 中山.
His son was in Zhōngshān 中山.
The ruler of Zhōngshān 中山 cooked his son
and sent him the soup.
Yuè Yáng 乐羊 sat under the tent and sipped it,
finishing one cup.
Marquis Wén 文侯 said to Dǔ Shī Zàn 堵师赞,
"Yuè Yáng 乐羊 ate his son's flesh because of me."
He replied,
"He ate his own son;
who else wouldn't he eat?"
Yuè Yáng 乐羊 withdrew from Zhōngshān 中山.
Marquis Wén 文侯 rewarded his achievement but suspected his intentions.
Mèng Sūn 孟孙 hunted and obtained a fawn.
He ordered Qín Xībā 秦西巴 to take it home,
its mother followed it, crying.
Qín Xībā 秦西巴 could not bear it and returned it to her.
Mèng Sūn 孟孙 returned
and asked for the fawn.
He replied,
"I couldn't bear it and gave it back to its mother."
Mèng Sūn 孟孙 was furious
He was driven away.
After living away for three months,
he was summoned again to be appointed as a tutor for his son.
His charioteer said:
"Previously, you were going to punish him,
but now you summon him to be a tutor for your son,
why is this?"
Mèng Sūn said:
"If I cannot bear to harm a fawn,
how much less could I bear to harm my own son?"
Therefore, it is said:
"Clever deceit is not as good as clumsy sincerity."
Yuè Yáng was viewed with suspicion despite having merit,
while Qín Xībā gained even more trust despite having committed a crime.
Zēng Cóngzǐ was
skilled at evaluating swords.
The ruler of Wèi resented the King of Wú.
Zēng Cóngzǐ said:
"The King of Wú loves swords,
and I am a sword evaluator.
I ask to evaluate swords for the King of Wú,
and draw one to show it to him,
and then take the opportunity to assassinate him for you."
The ruler of Wèi said:
"Your doing this
It is not for righteousness,
but for profit.
Wú is strong and rich,
Wèi is weak and poor.
You must go,
I fear you will be employed by the King of Wú against me."
And so he banished him.
Zhòu made ivory chopsticks, and Jī Zǐ sighed,
believing that ivory chopsticks
would certainly not be used to serve soup in earthenware pots,
but must be in cups of rhinoceros horn and jade;
if jade cups and ivory chopsticks
were not used to serve beans and greens,
then surely they must be served with rhinoceros tails, elephant tusks, and leopard fetuses.
If rhinoceros tails, elephant tusks, and leopard fetuses
were surely not eaten while wearing short hemp garments
and living under thatched roofs,
then surely they must be eaten wearing nine layers of brocade,
in high terraces and spacious rooms.
To satisfy such desires,
the world would not be enough.
A sage sees the subtle to know the bud,
sees the beginning to know the end.
Therefore, seeing ivory chopsticks, he sighed,
knowing the world would not be enough.
Zhōu Gōng Dàn 周公旦 having already defeated the Yin 殷,
was about to attack the city of Shānggài 商蓋.
Xīn Gōng Jiǎ 辛公甲 said:
"It is difficult to attack a large [state],
but easy to subdue a small one.
It is better to subdue the small ones to coerce the large one."
Thereupon, he attacked the nine Yí 夷 tribes, and Shānggài 商蓋 submitted.
Zhòu 紂 engaged in drinking throughout the long nights,
reveling to the point of losing track of the days.
He asked those around him,
but none of them knew either.
So he sent someone to ask Jī Zǐ 箕子.
Jī Zǐ 箕子 said to his followers:
"As the ruler of the realm,
if the entire country has lost track of the days,
the realm is in danger!
If the entire country does not know
and I alone know,
I am in danger."
He excused himself, saying he was drunk and did not know.
There was a man from Lǔ 魯 skilled at weaving shoes,
and his wife skilled at weaving fine silk,
and they wanted to move to Yuè 越.
Someone said to him:
"You will surely be impoverished."
A man of Lǔ said:
"What is the reason?"
He replied:
"Shoes are made to be worn,
but the people of Yuè walk barefoot;
white silk is for making caps,
but the people of Yuè let their hair hang loose.
To use your strengths
in a country that does not need them,
and expect endless success,
is that possible?"
Chén Zhěn was favored by the King of Wèi.
Huìzi said:
"You must treat those around the King well.
The willow tree,
planted horizontally, will live;
planted upside down, it will live;
broken and planted, it will still live.
However, if ten people plant it
and one person uproots it,
then no willow will live.
Even with the efforts of ten people
planting an easily grown thing,
they cannot overcome one person.
Why is that?
Planting is difficult,
but uprooting is easy.
Although you, sir, are skilled at establishing yourself with the King,
those who wish to remove you are many,
you will surely be in danger."
Jìsūn of Lǔ had just assassinated his ruler,
and Wú Qǐ took office there.
Someone said to Qǐ:
"The dead,
when they first die, bleed;
after bleeding, they become clotted blood;
after becoming clotted blood, they turn to ashes;
after turning to ashes, they become earth.
When they have become earth,
there is nothing that can be done.
Now, Jìsūn is only just beginning to bleed;
perhaps the future is still unknowable."
Thereupon, Wú Qǐ left and went to Jìn.
Xí Sīmí met with Tián Chéngzǐ.
Tián Chéngzǐ ascended a platform with him and looked out in all directions.
Three sides were unobstructed,
but looking south,
the trees of the Xí family obscured the view.
Tián Chéngzǐ did not say anything.
Xí Zǐ returned,
and sent someone to cut it down.
The axe made several cuts,
but Xí Zǐ stopped them.
His steward said:
"Why this change of heart?"
Xí Zǐ said:
"The ancients had a proverb that said:
'To know the fish in the deep is inauspicious.'
Master Tián is about to undertake a major endeavor,
and if I show him that I understand subtle matters,
I will certainly be in danger.
Not cutting down a tree
is no crime;
but to know what people do not say
is a great crime."
Therefore, he did not cut it down.
Yáng Zǐ stayed at an inn east of Sòng.
There were two concubines,
the ugly one was valued,
and the beautiful one was despised.
Yáng Zǐ asked the reason for this.
The innkeeper replied:
"The beautiful one prides herself on her beauty,
"I do not know what is beautiful;
the ugly are ugly of themselves;
I do not know what is ugly."
Yángzǐ 楊子 said to his disciples:
"Practicing virtue
and discarding the heart of self-proclaimed virtue,
where can you go that is not good?"
A man of Wèi 衛 married off his daughter and taught her, saying:
"Be sure to privately accumulate wealth.
To become someone's wife and then be sent away
is common.
To remain permanently
is fortunate."
His daughter accordingly privately accumulated wealth.
Her mother-in-law, thinking she was hoarding too much, sent her away.
The value of what his daughter brought back
doubled what she had taken when she married.
The father did not blame himself for teaching his daughter improperly,
but congratulated himself on knowing how to become richer.
Today, officials holding office
are all of this kind.
Lǔ Dān 魯丹 thrice persuaded the ruler of Zhōngshān 中山
without being accepted.
Thereupon, he scattered fifty gold pieces amongst his attendants.
He was seen again,
Before he spoke,
the ruler gave him food.
Lǔ Dān left,
and did not return to his lodging.
He then departed from Zhōngshān.
His charioteer said:
"He turned around to see you,
and only then did he treat me well.
Why are you leaving him?"
Lǔ Dān said:
"If he praises me because of someone's words,
he will surely condemn me because of someone's words."
Before he left the border,
the lord hated him, saying:
"He has come from Zhào to spy on Zhōngshān."
The ruler then sought him out and punished him.
Tián Bódǐng loved scholars and preserved his ruler;
Báigōng loved scholars and caused chaos in Jīng.
Their love of scholars was the same,
but what they did with it was different.
Gōngsūn Yǒu castrated himself to honor Bǎilǐ;
Shù Diāo castrated himself to flatter Duke Huán.
Their self-mutilation was the same,
but their reasons for self-mutilation were different.
Huìzǐ said:
"A madman runs eastward,
the pursuer also runs eastward.
Their eastward running is the same,
but the reason for their eastward running is different.
Therefore it is said:
'People doing the same thing
must be carefully examined.'"
Shuō Lín Xià, chapter twenty-three.
Bólè taught two men how to identify kicking horses,
and together they went to Jiǎnzǐ's stable to observe horses.
One person pointed out a kicking horse.
The other person followed behind and stroked it,
stroking its rump three times, but the horse did not kick.
This one thought he had lost the ability to identify such horses.
The other person said:
"You have not lost the ability to identify such horses.
The reason this horse is not kicking
is that it has a sprained shoulder and swollen knees.
Now, a kicking horse
raises its hindquarters and relies on its forequarters.
Swollen knees cannot bear the weight,
therefore the hindquarters are not raised.
You are skilled at identifying kicking horses
but unskilled at discerning swollen knees."
Now, affairs have an inevitable destination,
and to have a swollen knee and not be able to bear weight,
is something only the wise can discern.
Huìzi said:
"Put a monkey in a cage,
and it's the same as a pig."
Therefore, if the situation is unfavorable,
it is not a time to show off one's abilities.
General Wènzǐ of Wèi saw Zēngzǐ,
Zēngzǐ did not rise but invited him to sit on the mat,
straightening himself in the inner room.
Wènzǐ said to his driver:
"Zēngzǐ
is a foolish man!
If he takes me for a gentleman,
how can a gentleman not be respected?
If he takes me for a violent man,
how can a violent man be insulted?
That Zēngzǐ is not punished
is fate."
There is a bird that waddles clumsily,
heavy-headed and with a bent tail,
when it wants to drink from the river,
it is sure to topple over.
Therefore, it holds its feathers in its beak and drinks.
The reason why some people are not satisfied with drinking
is that you cannot but search for feathers (as a means of persuasion).
The *zhān* fish resembles a snake,
and the silkworm resembles a caterpillar.
People see a snake
and are terrified,
see a caterpillar
and their hair stands on end.
Fishermen hold *zhān* fish,
women gather silkworms;
where the profit lies,
everyone becomes like Bēn (賁) and Zhū (諸).
Bólè (伯樂) taught the person he hated how to judge thousand-league horses,
and taught the person he loved how to judge nag horses.
Thousand-league horses appear only occasionally,
so the profit is slow;
nag horses are sold daily,
so the profit is quick.
This is what the *Zhōu Shū* (周書) calls
"Those who speak below and are used above are
deluded."
Huán Hè (桓赫) said:
"In the art of carving,
nothing is better than a large nose,
Eyes are like small things.
A large nose can be made smaller,
but a small nose cannot be made larger;
small eyes can be made larger,
but large eyes cannot be made smaller."
Raising affairs is also like this:
If one does things for which there can be recovery afterward,
then affairs will have few failures.
Chóng Hóu and Èlái knew they would not escape Zhòu's punishment,
but did not foresee Wǔ Wáng's destruction of them.
Bǐ Gān and Zǐ Xū knew their rulers were certain to perish,
but did not know of their own deaths.
Therefore it is said:
"Chóng Hóu and Èlái knew the mind but did not understand the affair,
Bǐ Gān and Zǐ Xū understood the affair but did not understand the mind."
The sage is prepared for both.
The Song Tài Zǎi was powerful and held decisive authority.
Jì Zǐ was about to meet the ruler of Song,
and Liáng Zǐ heard of it and said:
"His words must be such that he is given a seat of equal rank with the Tài Zǎi,
if not,
he will not avoid trouble."
Therefore, Jì Zǐ spoke of honoring the ruler
and belittling the state.
Yáng Zhū's younger brother, Yáng Bù, went out wearing white clothes.
It rained.
Yáng Bù
took off his plain white clothes and put on black clothes to return home.
His dog did not recognize him and barked at him.
Yáng Bù was angry
and was about to strike it.
Yáng Zhū
said, "Don't strike it!
You are just the same.
If you had sent your dog out wearing white,
and it returned wearing black,
wouldn't you be surprised?"
Huìzi said:
"When Yì held the finger guard and arm guard,
held the bow and set the trigger,
the people of Yuè competed to hold the target for him.
But when a weak child pulls the bow,
a loving mother enters the house and closes the door."
Therefore, it is said:
"If it is certain,
then the people of Yuè will not doubt Yì;
if it is uncertain,
then a loving mother will flee from a weak child."
Duke Huán
asked Guǎn Zhòng:
He replied:
"Water that has a limit
Wealth that has a limit
If a person cannot stop themselves at sufficiency
is water that has no more.
is wealth that is already sufficient.
and perishes, 豈 (qǐ)
isn't that the limit of wealth!"
In the state of Sòng, there was a wealthy merchant named Jiān Zhǐzi,
who competed with someone to buy a hundred-gold piece of uncut jade.
He then pretended to lose it and destroyed it,
shouldered the loss of his hundred gold,
and processed the damaged flaws,
obtaining over a thousand in profit.
There are matters that, when undertaken, end in failure,
and people consider it wise not to undertake them;
it is a matter of timing.
There was someone who wanted to use his skill in charioteering to be presented to the King of Jīng,
but the other grooms were jealous of him.
Therefore, he said:
"Your servant can shoot deer while driving."
He was presented to the king.
The king drove first,
and did not hit a deer;
when he drove himself,
Reached it.
The king praised his driving skills,
then said that the other grooms were jealous of him.
The son of the magistrate of Jīng was about to attack Chén.
An old man saw him off, saying:
"Jìn is strong,
you must be careful."
The son of the magistrate said:
"What are you worried about, old man?
I will destroy Jìn for you."
The old man said:
"Agreed.
I will be lodging outside the south gate of Chén."
The son of the magistrate said:
"What is the reason for this?"
He said:
"I am laughing at Gōujiàn.
Doing things for others is so easy,
why did he alone struggle secretly for ten difficult years?"
Yáo yielded the world to Xǔ Yóu,
Xǔ Yóu fled from it,
lodged at his family's house,
and his family hid his leather cap.
To abandon the world
and have his family hide his leather cap,
This is not understanding Xǔ Yóu 許由.
Three lice were arguing with each other.
One louse passed by them,
and said:
"What are you arguing about?"
The three lice said:
"We are fighting over a rich and fertile land."
The one louse said:
"Are you not also worried about the arrival of the winter sacrifice [là 臘]
and the dryness of the thatch?
What else are you worried about?"
Thereupon, they gathered together and sucked their mother
and ate her.
The pig became thin,
so people did not kill it.
There is an insect called guì 螝,
one body with two mouths,
competing for food and biting each other.
Consequently, they killed each other,
and thus committed suicide.
Those ministers who fight over affairs and lose their countries
are all of the guì 螝 kind.
If a palace has whitewash and
vessels have washing,
then it is clean.
Conducting oneself is also like this;
if there is no place to wash the white mud,
then there will be few faults.
Gōngzǐ Jiū was about to cause chaos,
Duke Huán sent a messenger to observe him.
The messenger reported, saying:
"His laughter is not joyful,
his vision is unfocused,
he will surely cause chaos."
Thereupon, he had the people of Lǔ kill him.
Gōngsūn Hóng cut off his hair and became a horseman for the King of Yuè,
Gōngsūn Xǐ sent someone to sever relations with him, saying:
"I will no longer be a brother to you."
Gōngsūn Hóng said:
"I cut off my hair,
you will have your head cut off and be used by others in war;
what am I to say to you?"
In the battle of Zhōu Nán,
Gōngsūn Xǐ died there.
Someone lived next to a violent person,
wanting to sell his house and avoid him.
Someone said:
"It is because his evil deeds are about to be full."
"Okay,
you just wait for him."
He replied:
"I fear that he will fill his deeds with me."
Therefore, he left.
Thus, it is said:
"Those who perceive the underlying principles of things
are not misled by external appearances."
Kǒngzǐ said to his disciples,
"Who can guide Zǐxī in his pursuit of fame through fishing?"
Zǐgòng said,
"Cì can."
He then guided him,
and he no longer had doubts.
Kǒngzǐ said,
"How generous!
He is not swayed by personal gain.
How pure!
The nature of the people is constant.
What is crooked is crooked,
what is straight is straight."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Zǐxī will not escape harm."
During the Rebellion of Báigōng,
Zǐxī died.
Therefore it is said,
"Those who are upright in their actions are devious in their desires."
Jìn Zhōngxíng Wénzǐ (晉中行文子) fled into exile and
passed through a district.
A follower said:
"This is a stingy fellow,
an old acquaintance of yours, my lord.
Why don't you rest and lodge here,
and wait for the carriages behind?"
Wénzǐ (文子) said:
"I once liked music,
and this man gave me a zither;
I liked ornaments,
and this man gave me a jade ring.
These are the ones who flaunt my faults.
He seeks favor with me,
and I fear that he will use me to seek favor with others."
So he left him.
As a result, he indeed seized two carriages belonging to Wénzǐ's (文子) rear guard
and presented them to his lord.
Zhōu Zào (周趮) said to Gōng Tā (宮他):
"Say this to the King of Qí (齊):
'If Qí (齊) provides me with resources in Wèi (魏),
I will serve the King with Wèi (魏).'"
Gōng Tā (宮他) said:
"That won't do.
This demonstrates that he is without Wèi.
The King of Qí will certainly not rely on one without Wèi,
but will resent one who possesses Wèi.
Your Grace might as well say:
"According to what Your Majesty desires,
your servant requests to use Wèi to listen to Your Majesty."
The King of Qí will certainly consider Your Grace as possessing Wèi,
and will certainly rely on Your Grace.
This is Your Grace possessing Qí.
Relying on this, Your Grace will possess Qí
and Wèi."
Bái Guī said to the Grand Magistrate of Sòng:
"The ruler himself understands government,
Your Grace has no duties.
Now the ruler is young and pursues reputation,
it would be better to have Jīng congratulate the ruler on his filial piety.
Then the ruler will not seize Your Grace's position,
and will greatly respect and value Your Grace,
then Your Grace will always employ Sòng."
Guǎn Zhòng and Bào Shū said to each other:
"The ruler is extremely disordered,
he will certainly lose the state.
Among the various noble sons of the state of Qí, those who can be assisted
are either Gōngzǐ Jiū
or Xiǎobái.
"Each of you shall serve one person.
The one who achieves success first should assist the other."
Guǎn Zhòng then followed Gōngzǐ Jiū,
Bào Shū followed Xiǎobái.
The people of the state indeed assassinated their ruler.
Xiǎobái entered the state first and became the ruler.
The people of Lǔ arrested Guǎn Zhòng and delivered him.
Bào Shū spoke on his behalf and served as his minister.
Therefore, the proverb says:
"Even though Wū Xián is good at praying,
he cannot cleanse himself.
Even though the doctor of Qín is good at healing,
he cannot cure himself."
Even with the wisdom of Guǎn Zhòng,
he still awaited Bào Shū's assistance.
This is what the vulgar proverb means when it says,
"A barbarian selling his own fur coat cannot sell it,
A scholar praising his own eloquence is not believed."
The King of Jīng attacked Wú.
Wú sent Jǔ Wèi and Jué Róng to犒the army of Jīng,
and the general said:
"Bind them,
and kill them to consecrate the drums."
He asked them,
"Woman, come,
will you divine?"
She replied:
"I will divine."
"Will the divination be auspicious?"
She said:
"Auspicious."
A person from Jīng said:
"Now Jīng intends to use you to consecrate the drums with blood,
what is the reason for this?"
She replied:
"This is the reason why it is auspicious.
Wú sent people to come,
they are specifically watching for the general's anger.
If the general is angry,
he will dig deep trenches and build high ramparts;
if the general is not angry,
he will be lax.
Now,
if the general kills me,
then Wú will surely be on high alert.
Moreover, the divination of a state
is not done for one subject.
Now, killing one subject to save a state,
why should it not be called auspicious?
Why is that?
Moreover, if the dead have no knowledge,
then using a subject to smear the drum with blood would be of no benefit;
if the dead have knowledge,
then the subject would ensure that the drum does not sound
when the subject is about to fight."
The Jīng people therefore did not kill him.
Zhì Bó was about to attack Chóu Yóu,
but the road was difficult and impassable.
So he cast a large bell and gifted it to the ruler of Chóu Yóu.
The ruler of Chóu Yóu was greatly pleased
and cleared the road to bring it in.
Chìzhāng Mànzhī said:
"This is not permissible.
This is how a small state serves a large one,
and now that the large one is coming,
the soldiers will surely follow.
It cannot be allowed in."
The ruler of Chóu Yóu did not listen
and allowed it in.
Chìzhāng Mànzhī then broke the axle of his carriage and fled,
reaching Qí.
In the seventh month, Chóu Yóu was destroyed.
After Yúe had defeated Wú,
Then he demanded soldiers from Jīng (荊) to attack Jìn (晉).
The Left Historiographer Yǐ Xiàng (倚相) said to the King of Jīng (荊):
"When Yè (越) defeated Wú (吳),
the valiant warriors died,
the elite soldiers were exhausted,
and the heavily armored troops were injured.
Now, you are again demanding soldiers to attack Jìn (晉),
showing that we are not weakened.
It would be better to raise an army and share Wú (吳)."
The King of Jīng (荊) said:
"Good."
Thereupon, he raised an army and followed Yè (越).
The King of Yè (越) was angered
and prepared to attack him.
Grand Master Zhǒng (種) said:
"It is not advisable.
Our valiant warriors are exhausted,
and our heavily armored troops are injured.
If we fight with them,
we will surely not be victorious.
It is better to bribe them."
Then, they ceded five hundred *lǐ* (里) of the shaded side of Mount Lù (露山)
as a bribe.
Jīng (荊) attacked Chén (陳),
and Wú (吳) came to its rescue,
The armies were thirty *lǐ* apart.
It rained for ten days.
At night, the stars were visible.
The Left Historian, Yǐ Xiàng (倚相), said to Zǐ Qī (子期):
"It has rained for ten days.
The armor is being prepared and the soldiers are gathering.
The people of Wú (吳) must be coming.
It is better to prepare for them."
So he arranged a formation.
Before the formation was complete, the Wú (吳) people arrived.
Seeing the Chǔ (楚) formation, they retreated.
The Left Historian said:
"Wú (吳) retreated sixty *lǐ*.
Their gentlemen must be resting.
Their commoners must be eating.
If we travel thirty *lǐ* to attack them,
we can certainly defeat them."
So they followed his advice.
and then broke the Wú (吳) army.
Hán (韓) and Zhào (趙) were at odds with each other.
The ruler of Hán (韓) requested soldiers from Wèi (魏), saying:
"I wish to borrow troops to attack Zhào (趙)."
Marquis Wén of Wèi (魏文侯) said:
"I am brothers with Zhào (趙).
I cannot comply."
Zhào also requested soldiers to attack Hán.
Wén Hóu said,
"I am brothers with Hán,
and I dare not comply."
The two states could not obtain soldiers,
and they angrily turned against him.
Afterwards, they realized Wén Hóu was using them to scheme,
so they all paid tribute to Wèi.
Qí attacked Lǔ,
demanding the Chán Ding cauldron,
and Lǔ sent a goose in its place.
The people of Qí said,
"It is a goose."
The people of Lǔ said,
"It is genuine."
Qí said,
"If Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn comes,
I will listen to you."
The ruler of Lǔ requested Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn to come,
and Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn said,
"Why not send the genuine one?"
The ruler said,
"I cherish it."
He replied,
"I also cherish my trustworthiness."
Hán Jiū 韩咎 was established as ruler, but it was not yet settled.
His younger brother was in Zhōu 周.
Zhōu 周 wanted to value him highly,
but feared that Hán Jiū 韩咎 would not be established.
Qímǔ Huī 綦母恢 said:
"It would be better to send him off with a hundred chariots.
If he is established,
then claim it is for defense;
if he is not established,
then say he has come to surrender the rebels."
Jìngguō Jūn 靖郭君 was about to build a city in Xuē 薛,
and many guests tried to dissuade him.
Jìngguō Jūn 靖郭君 said to the gatekeeper:
"Do not let any guests through."
A man from Qí 齐 requested an audience, saying:
"I only ask to speak three words.
If I exceed three words,
I ask to be boiled."
Therefore, Jìngguō Jūn 靖郭君 granted him an audience.
The guest hurried forward and said:
"Big fish of the sea."
Then he turned and ran away.
Jìngguō Jūn 靖郭君 said:
"Please tell me the meaning."
The guest said:
"Your servant dares not jest with death."
Jìng Guō Jūn said:
"I wish you would speak to me about it."
He replied:
"Has Your Lordship heard of the great fish?
Nets cannot stop it,
and arrows cannot snag it.
But once it is stranded and loses water,
even ants will be pleased.
Now, the state of Qí is also Your Lordship's sea.
If Your Lordship maintains possession of Qí,
what need is there for Xuē?
But if Your Lordship loses Qí,
even if you build the walls of Xuē as high as the sky,
it will still be of no benefit."
Jìng Guō Jūn said:
"Good."
Thereupon he ceased,
and did not fortify Xuē.
The younger brother of the King of Jīng was in Qín,
but Qín would not release him.
A gentleman of the middle ranks said:
"Give me a hundred gold pieces,
and I will be able to get him out."
Because he carried a hundred *jīn* to Jìn,
he saw Shū Xiàng and
said:
"The King of Jīng's younger brother is in Qín,
and Qín will not release him.
Please allow me to entrust these hundred *jīn* to Shū Xiàng."
Shū Xiàng received the *jīn*
and used it to see Duke Píng of Jìn, saying:
"We can build a city at Húqiū."
Duke Píng said:
"Why?"
He replied:
"The King of Jīng's younger brother is in Qín,
and Qín will not release him.
This means that Qín dislikes Jīng,
and they will certainly not dare to forbid us from building a city at Húqiū.
If they forbid it,
we will say:
'Release the King of Jīng's younger brother for me,
and we will not build the city.'
If they release him,
we can gain favor with Jīng;
if they do not release him,
it shows their complete dislike,
and they will certainly not dare to forbid us from building a city at Húqiū."
The Duke said:
"Good."
So he fortified Húqiū.
He said to the Duke of Qín:
"If you release the younger brother of the King of Jīng for me,
I will not fortify it."
Qín therefore released him.
The King of Jīng was very pleased
and presented Jìn with a hundred yì of refined gold.
Hé Lǘ attacked Yǐng,
winning three battles.
He asked Zǐxū:
"Is it possible to retreat?"
Zǐxū replied:
"If one who is drowning is allowed to stop after one drink,
then there will be no one who is successfully drowned,
because of the rest.
It is better to take advantage of the situation to submerge him."
A man of Zhèng had a son
who was about to become an official.
He said to his family:
"You must repair the dilapidated wall;
it is not good,
people will steal."
The neighbor in the alley also said the same.
When he did not constantly repair it,
people indeed stole from it.
He considered his son wise,
and regarded the person who reported it (the theft) in the neighborhood as a thief.
*Guān Xíng* (Observing Conduct), Chapter Twenty-Four
The people of ancient times
had eyes too short to see themselves,
therefore they used a mirror to view their faces;
their wisdom was too short to know themselves,
therefore they used the Dao to correct themselves.
Therefore, a mirror has no blame for revealing flaws,
and the Dao has no resentment for illuminating faults.
If the eyes lose the mirror,
they have no way to correct their beard and eyebrows;
if the body loses the Dao,
it has no way to know its confusion.
Xīmén Bào's 西門豹 nature was hasty,
therefore he wore soft leather to slow himself down;
Dǒng Ān yú's 董安于 heart was slow,
therefore he wore a bowstring to urge himself on.
Therefore, using what is in excess to supplement what is insufficient,
and using what is long to extend what is short
is what is called an enlightened ruler.
There are three certainties in the world:
First, there are things that wisdom cannot accomplish.
Second, there are things that strength cannot lift.
Third, there are things that force cannot overcome.
Therefore, even if one possesses the wisdom of Yáo 堯,
without the assistance of the masses,
great achievements cannot be established.
If one possesses the might of Wū Huò 烏獲,

If one possesses the strength of Bēn 賁 and Yù 育,

Thus, Wū Huò 烏獲 can lift a thousand *jūn* 鈞 with ease,

It's not that his body is heavier than a thousand *jūn* 鈞,

Lí Zhū 離朱 easily hits targets a hundred paces away,

It's not that a hundred paces is close while eyebrows and eyelashes are far,

nor does he trouble Lí Zhū 離朱
Because it cannot see itself.
Relying on circumstance and power,

Time has fullness and emptiness,

The unadorned essence of sages and worthies is profound.
Therefore, a wise ruler observes others,

Understanding that Yáo cannot achieve success alone,

with laws and methods,

*Ān Wēi* (Security and Danger), Chapter Twenty-Five.
There are seven techniques for security,
and six paths to danger.
Techniques for security:
First:
Rewards and punishments follow right and wrong;
Second:
Fortune and misfortune follow good and evil.
Three:
Life and death follow the law.
Four:
There is worthiness and unworthiness, but no love or hate.
Five:
There is foolishness and wisdom, but no unwarranted praise or blame.
Six:
There are set measures (chǐ cùn), but no arbitrary estimations (yì dù).
Seven:
There is trustworthiness (xìn) and no deception (zhà).
Dangerous paths:
One:
To hew and carve within the confines of the plumb line (zhú xuē yú shéng zhī nèi).
Two:
To sever and cut outside the bounds of the law (duàn gē yú fǎ zhī wài).
Three:
To benefit (lì) people in what harms them.
Four:
To rejoice in what brings misfortune to others.
Five:
To endanger people in what they rely on for security.
Six:
Those you love are not close to you.
Those you hate are not kept at a distance.
If this is the case,
then people lose what makes life enjoyable
and forget what makes death serious.
If people do not enjoy life,
then the ruler is not respected.
If they do not take death seriously,

If everyone in the world exhausts their intelligence on ceremonial appearances

There will be few petty people and many gentlemen.
Therefore, the altars of the state will stand long

There is no Zhòng Ní 仲尼 on a runaway chariot,

Therefore, commands and decrees

When they are secure, wisdom and integrity arise.
When they are in danger, contention and baseness arise.
Therefore, the method of securing a country
is like eating when hungry
When cold, one puts on clothes;

The former kings entrusted principles to bamboo and silk;

Now, if one compels people to forsake hunger and cold,

If one abandons what is natural,

If even the strong and brave cannot accomplish something,

If the ruler above insatiably demands what is already exhausted,

With nothing,

The law is what makes a state,

It is said that in ancient times, Biǎn Què (扁鵲) treated illnesses

Piercing bones

to reject advice,

Thus, a person who is severely ill

Enduring pain,

rejecting advice,

Being ill but not enduring pain,

being in danger but not rejecting advice,

If the ruler does not discipline himself like Yáo,

If Yáo 堯 and Shùn 舜 are deposed and Jié 桀 and Zhòu 紂 are established,

Safety and danger lie in right and wrong,

survival and extinction lie in substance and emptiness,

When names and realities do not match,

Jié, the Son of Heaven,

A wise ruler solidifies the internal,

The way of a wise ruler is to be loyal to the law,

They leave and are missed.
Yáo had no adhesive pact with his contemporaries,

To establish the Dao in times past

Chapter Twenty-Six: Upholding the Dao.

Ministers in a well-governed age

fighting like Biàn and Yù,

The ruler can be content and at ease within the Jade Hall,

To subdue a tiger without a cage,

In the present age,

Comprehending the feelings of Bēn (賁) and Yù (育),

I have heard that those in ancient times who were good at employing people

If it is like this,

Lighten their responsibilities,

An enlightened ruler ensures that affairs do not interfere with each other,

When disputes and lawsuits cease,

Abandoning law and methods and governing with the heart,

Discarding compasses and squares and relying on arbitrary estimations,

Then you will not fail in ten thousand cases.
The ruler of men,

The ancients said:

A ruler who abandons the three easily understood methods,

I have heard it said:
Even Yáo could not find someone who undertakes affairs without causing trouble."

To not investigate matters within one's private household,

Not removing the disaster at one's eyebrows and eyelashes

In the present age,

There are four things by which an enlightened ruler establishes merit

Without opportunity from Heaven,

Therefore, obtaining opportunity from Heaven

obtaining the hearts of the people

relying on skill and ability

obtaining power and position
Then there is no need to push forward, yet fame is achieved.
Like water flowing,
like a boat floating.
Adhering to the way of nature,

thus it is said:

Chapter 29: The Grand Design
The ancients who fully grasped the grand design:
contemplated heaven and earth,
observed rivers and seas,
followed mountains and valleys,
(considered) where the sun and moon shine,
(and) the movements of the four seasons,
the spreading of clouds and the movement of wind.
They did not burden their minds with cleverness,
nor encumber themselves with selfishness.
They entrusted governance and disorder to laws and methods,
relied on rewards and punishments for right and wrong,
and assigned importance to scales and weights.
They did not go against the principles of heaven,
nor harm human nature;
they did not blow on hairs to find tiny flaws,
nor wash off grime to examine the hard-to-know;
they did not pull (the string) beyond the plumb line,
Do not push within the constraints of the rope;
do not hasten beyond the bounds of the law,
nor be slow within the bounds of the law;
uphold established principles,
follow natural courses;
misfortune and fortune arise from the Dao and the law,
and do not come from love or hate;
responsibility for honor and disgrace lies within oneself,
and not within others.
Therefore, in an era of utmost peace,
the law is like morning dew,
pure simplicity does not dissipate,
hearts have no knotted resentments,
mouths have no vexatious words.
Therefore, carriages and horses are not exhausted by long journeys,
banners and flags are not disordered in great marshes,
the myriad people do not lose their lives to bandits and soldiers,
heroes and valiant men do not prolong their lives by flagpoles and banners;
outstanding individuals do not have their names recorded in books,
nor are their merits inscribed on *pányú* (vessels),
